He should be here by now. I was pretty clear about meeting at 5:30pm.
It’s already 5:45pm and he isn’t even in sight. I thought for sure that he wouldn’t miss a chance to meet up with me again.
I can’t contain my nerves. I try to tell myself that I’m only angry because of trepidation, and I’m not actually angry at him.
This is a big moment for me. I’ve never once revealed my identity to anyone.
I assume he will take it in stride. I wouldn’t be going through with this if I didn’t firmly believe that.
My neck jerks in reaction to the voice.
“There you are.”
“I’m late?”
I make a point of checking the time on my phone and nod.
“Soz. Traffic?”
“You drove here?”
“What did you want to discuss?”
“I have a request for you. And… A confession.”
Kojiro’s eyes widen and he looks me up and down.
“Knew it…”
I blink and look down at the ground.
He’s known for some time. I was fooling myself thinking that my stupid attempts to erase suspicion of my identity were working on him.
“You’re going to confess your love… Been waiting for this moment.”
“Wait…! No, that’s not—”
“Shh. No more words. I accept your heart.”
“Kojiro, I don’t—”
“Call me Koji now. We’re one. No need to be shy.”
This isn’t getting me anywhere.
Thanks to my frustration and nervousness, I simply blurt out my true confession.
“I’m Corpse Girl.”
Kojiro doesn’t react. Well, he cocks his head a few degrees to the side, slowly and surely. If you can even call that a reaction to my sudden outburst.
“Yes? Okay. So… A kiss to commemorate our love?”
“Did you even hear what I just said?”
“I’m Corpse Girl! I’m the one behind the corpse photos, and the deaths, and…”
It feels kind of strange to say these things out loud. For some reason it leaves a sour and bitter taste in my mouth that I can’t swallow.
“Yes. I know.”
“Knew it since our first noise chat.”
“Our first noise chat…?”
“Remember? You messaged me late at night. Asked me if I knew about Corpse Girl.”
“Is that what tipped you off? You assumed I was her just because I mentioned her?”
“Then… How? How did you figure it out?”
“You asked me to look up names. Names of Corpse Girl’s victims.”
“Oh, yeah. I did, huh… That was stupid of me.”
“I suppose that gave it away.”
“Other people could have known those names.”
“Then… Come on. Throw me a bone here. How’d you find out?”
“You said you requested Eiichi Hanada’s death.”
Eiichi Hanada. The guy who died in a traffic accident.
I remember that I lied to Kojiro about being the one to request his death. It was the only way I could escape his suspicions at the time.
If I remember correctly, it threw him off my trail for a while.
He believed I was the one who requested the death, so that explained how I knew he was one of Corpse Girl’s victims.
But if what Kojiro is telling me now is true, then my lie actually had the opposite effect. How did it make him figure out my identity?
“I don’t understand. I confessed to requesting Eiichi Hanada’s death. So what?”
“That was a lie.”
“Even so, I still don’t understand.”
“You’re not making any sense.”
Kojiro’s shoulders drop. He stares at me intently.
“You lied about requesting Eiichi Hanada’s death.”
“That lie proved to me that you’re Corpse Girl.”
“Yes, but how?! Tell me!”
“I was the one who requested Eiichi Hanada’s death.”
Kojiro’s deadpan countenance makes his claim believable beyond all doubt.
I feel the blood drain from my face.
“I submitted his photo to Corpse Girl’s website.”
“Imagine my surprise when you claimed that you did it.”
“That lie made it clear. You knew his name. You knew he died.”
“You knew he was Corpse Girl’s victim.”
“Ergo… You are Corpse Girl.”
Despite my dazed state, I can’t fault his logic. I took credit for something Kojiro did—of course that would paint me as a liar in his eyes.
“So… You’ve known this whole time.”
“And yet… You still met up with me. Not just today. But at the cafe, too.”
“Aren’t you… scared of me…?”
“Ah ha ha!”
“No. That’s not the way I’d put it.”
“You should be scared of me. After all, I requested the death.”
“Had motive for murder… Even if I didn’t carry it out personally.”
“Imagine what else I’m capable of.”
I subconsciously take a step back from Kojiro’s suddenly looming form.
“From our discussions, I know you don’t kill your victims.”
“You just nudge them. Urge them. Tempt them with death as an escape from their fear.”
“You’re no murderer. What reason have I to fear you?”
He’s right… He’s absolutely right. He knows everything about Corpse Girl’s methods. My methods.
Kojiro is a dangerous enemy.
Or a powerful ally.
And it’s up to me to decide whether he’s with me or against me.
I recall our conversation at the cafe. He claimed he would support Corpse Girl if she came to him for assistance. He’s a fan.
He would support her obediently, no questions asked… as long as the price was right.
So, all I have to do is make him an offer that he can’t refuse.
“Join me.”
“Help me... Help Corpse Girl rid this fucking world of the fetid filth that infests it.”
I decide to quote a certain passage from a book that Kojiro himself gave me. A paragraph from ‘Strange Flower’ that has stuck with me for some time.
“‘There’s a certain beauty in death. A macabre certainty, an absolute state of finality.’”
“Nobel Sinclaire…”
“You understand what I’m talking about. You work with cadavers for a living.”
“The dead can’t hurt you. They can’t betray you. They can’t disobey, or object, or disapprove.”
“Wouldn’t it be better if we were all beautiful like that?”
“Didn’t expect Corpse Girl to be so vain.”
“Is your motivation simply to impart your own ideas of beauty to the world?”
“There’s more to it?”
“Of course. I, me, myself, Noriko, may be vain. But Corpse Girl isn’t burdened by such petty notions. Her ambition is pure.”
“Her ambition is crucial to the survival of the entire human race.”
“Ah ha…”
“Thought I had a big ego.”
“You’re so self-important. Both you and Corpse Girl.”
“I don’t expect you to understand. Not yet.”
“But… I’ve realized that I can’t do everything alone.”
“I need your help. I need cadavers.”
“I see.”
“What’s in it for me?”
This is the critical point of our negotiation.
It could all fall apart here if I don’t offer something that Kojiro considers worth the risk.
The question is, what does he want? What does he desire?
“I propose an equal partnership. You’ll reap half of the benefits from Corpse Girl’s work.”
This offer is a gamble, and I know that in the back of my mind. However, it was the only feasible solution I could come up with when I planned out this encounter late last night.
This tactic relies completely on my assumed understanding of Kojiro’s innermost desires. If I’m wrong about him, then… This whole thing will blow up in my face.
“Corpse Girl will create more death than you could ever imagine. Think of all the fresh corpses you could get your eager little hands on.”
Kojiro shakes his head, his lips pursed in a thin line of disapproval.
“Sorry. Already got my fill of corpses.”
“Morgue’s full enough as it is.”
I narrow my eyes and stand my ground. I can’t back down now. I’m so close to unraveling him and his secrets.
“You’ve always wanted to mimic Nobel Sinclaire. I can see it in your face, in your very soul, whenever you praise his work.”
“You want to emulate his actions and experience his escapades firsthand.”
“You want to dress up corpses, take them out to dinner, perform all manner of bizarre social experiments with the dead…”
“It’s your passion. But living vicariously through Nobel Sinclaire’s books isn’t enough for you anymore.”
“And that’s where your fascination with me—with Corpse Girl—stems from.”
“As soon as you figured me out, you knew I was your gateway to satisfying your lust for the macabre.”
“You work with cadavers all day, every day… But you can’t get them out of the morgue with eyes on you at all times.”
“But I can.”
“I have the perfect plan on how to withdraw all the corpses we could ever need. Half of them for you, and half of them for me.”
“An equal partnership.”
I end my speech and let Kojiro bask in my words.
I hope I was convincing enough to sway him. And I hope, I pray, that I’m correct about his sickest desires.
His reaction isn’t exactly what I was expecting.
He laughs, a big, hearty guffaw that scares a few nearby birds and sends them flying to safety.
Clapping his hands together slowly, he inches closer to me until I can feel his breath across my face.
“Figured me out?”
“I’ll play along.”
“Say there’s a way to get corpses out of the morgue. Without getting busted. Don’t you think I’d have found it by now?”
“Perhaps you’re not as clever as you think you are.”
“Ah ha. Perhaps.”
“But you have the answer?”
“I do. I guarantee it will work.”
A bead of sweat forms on the back of my neck. I’m not exactly bluffing, because I have planned out this whole scenario in detail.
But until I actually try to pull off such a maneuver, I can only speculate that it will work. I need to exaggerate my confidence long enough for us to rally together.
“Hmm. Something about you makes you seem trustworthy.”
“So be it.”
“Consider us partners. For now.”
“You accept?”
“Sure. Don’t make me regret it.”
“But, listen.”
“What I do with my share of corpses is my business. No nosing about. Got it?”
“You still want to keep secrets, even if we’ll be working together?”
“Shouldn’t we be open and honest and build a trusting partnership?”
“Here’s the deal. You don’t pry, and I’ll assist you with Corpse Girl’s work.”
“I’ll help you craft your elaborate photos. No charge.”
“I get privacy. You get an assistant.”
“Mutually beneficial, wouldn’t you agree?”
I think about his offer. It’s true that I don’t really need to know what he’s going to do with the corpses on offer.
The whole thing is illegal already. So if he wants to take it further, that’s not on me.
And if I can get some assistance, it will surely help me churn out photos at a faster rate.
I’ll need muscle to move bodies, for starters. That alone is worth keeping my nose clean.
“Okay. We have a deal.”
“Glad to hear it.”
Kojiro extends a hand and I grip it as firmly as my frail bones will allow.
We shake once, and Kojiro offers me a surprisingly warm smile. His intense, murderous demeanor suddenly vanishes and he reverts to his awkward, alien self.
“Soz about the love confession stuff before.”
“Too late now, but… I’d have helped Corpse Girl in return for a simple date.”
Seriously…? Did I come up with some elaborate insight into his psyche and his desires for absolutely no reason? Was all he wanted a chance to take me out?
“Ah ha…”
“No backing out now. We’ve got a deal, right?”
“Right. Welcome to the team, Kojiro.”
“Team Corpse Girl, huh. Well, it’s good to be on board.”
“My morgue connection, your schemes…”
“We hoist piles of corpses out and split the stack fifty-fifty. That the whole of it?”
“To put it simply, yeah. And I get your assistance with Corpse Girl’s work. A reward for keeping my eyes shut.”
“‘Course. Looking forward to that.”
“A spoken contract’s as good as anything to me. I’m satisfied.”
“When do we start?”
“Soon. There’s only one thing missing from my plan.”
“That is?”
“We need somewhere to store the bodies we retrieve.”
“Somewhere big, with no one to meddle in our business.”
“I’m thinking an old warehouse or something like that.”
“A warehouse, huh?”
“What about an abandoned factory? I might know a place.”
“A factory…?”
An abandoned factory, all for our corpse collection.
I like the sound of that…
It’s pretty late by the time I get back home. I’m completely wiped out.
That conversation with Kojiro took way more out of me than I would have guessed.
My entire mouth feels parched and dry, probably due to a combination of nervousness and talking far too much.
Still… I’m happy with the end result. That meeting was worth stepping out of my comfort zone for.
I’ll wait for Kojiro to get back to me about the abandoned factory. Once we secure a location like that, our real work will begin.
I figure that I should turn in for the night since I need to be at the office in the morning.
But the ever-present tug of curiosity pulls at my sleeve, and I feel myself being drawn to my laptop.
I’ll take a quick look for new requests. Just a peek.
Laptop open and logged in, I feel a surge of endorphins slug me across the face when I see the notification for one new request.
Squealing like an overly excited schoolgirl, I open the message and view the details.
REQUEST DETAILS:
Today, 6:02pm (local time)
Victim’s Phone: (**)***-***-***
Downloading image attachment...
The photo loads almost instantly and fills the screen.
A woman, middle-aged, with a stern expression. Well-groomed and dressed in business attire.
And immediately familiar.
Kotomi Ida…
I’m in complete disbelief.
Seeing this request come through the site gives me a disorienting sense of déjà vu. I rack my brain for the cause, wondering if I’ve lived this moment before.
The answer hits me quickly despite my mind’s exhaustion.
Kotomi Ida isn’t the first coworker of mine to have her death requested.
Though I didn’t know at the time, Akane Tsurumaki also worked in my building—and her death was requested not all that long ago.
Kotomi Ida marks the second person to be wanted dead within my company. And, she’s an exec—just like Tsurumaki.
I wonder if this is simply a coincidence? It surely has to be. After all, Tomoe confessed that she was the one to request Tsurumaki’s death. And she seemed to regret doing so.
Therefore, I have to doubt that she’d go on to upload Kotomi Ida’s photo to the site.
So, who could want Kotomi Ida dead…?
She isn’t the most likable person, but who really is?
She deals with the juniors on my floor on a regular basis. The juniors, like me, Tomoe, Shinya…
That’s right. Thanks to Kotomi, Shinya’s prospects at the company are dead in the dirt. And that’s before even diving into the true issue—their current relationship.
Would he request her death as retribution? He doesn’t seem like the type, but…
I let out a sigh. I’m far too tired to run through the myriad possibilities tonight.
I don’t think I can even bring my weary fingers to navigate to the Database of the Deceased to start on this request.
I’ll tackle this tomorrow. No matter the reasons behind the request, Kotomi Ida will receive a corpse photo.
That’s my conviction as Corpse Girl, after all.
I close the lid of my laptop and throw myself down on the bed, begging for sleep to claim me quickly.
Text_Month="June 10";Text_Day="WEDNESDAY";Text_Time="Morning"
“I need to talk to you.”
“What’s with that look? Got somethin’ up yer ass?”
“Come on. Just follow me.”
I grab Tomoe’s wrist and guide her away from the labyrinth of desks and into the elevator waiting patiently for us.
We emerge from the double-doors into the lobby.
The place is quiet and nearly empty. It offers significantly more privacy than the crowded fourteenth floor.
“Gawd, yer fingers are bony. Yer pinchin’ me.”
I let go of her wrist and she rubs it gingerly against her clothes.
“Anyway, what’s up?”
I hesitate for a moment. Even though I ran through this scenario in my head during the train ride, I’m still anxious about playing it out now.
But, this situation involves Tomoe, either directly or indirectly. As my friend, she needs to know.
“I think Corpse Girl is going to target Kotomi Ida.”
“Did she get one of them photos?”
Her reaction is fairly indifferent. I thought after being involved in Tsurumaki’s death, this news would have more of an impact on her.
“Well, no, I don’t think so, but…”
“How d’yeh know, then?”
“That’s hard to explain. Just bear with me.”
“Kotomi and Shinya had a falling out. Because of her, his career here is at an end. I’m sure he told you about it.”
That makes sense. Shinya would confide in his girlfriend about his career, but… I don’t know the extent of Tomoe’s inside knowledge.
I doubt she knows the true nature of their relationship, judging by how nonchalant her reaction has been so far.
“So… If you can kind of guess what I’m getting at…”
“I think, maybe, that Shinya requested her death.”
“Ah ha! Shinya? Nah, he don’t have it in him.”
“Besides, that bitch has it comin’.”
“She does…?”
“Yep. I’m surprised yeh found out ‘bout it, but…”
“I plugged her photo into Corpse Girl’s website yesterday.”
I’m stunned. I can hardly formulate a response to Tomoe’s confession.
“Absolute skank… She deserves to die.”
“But… Why…? After you requested Akane Tsurumaki’s death, why would you…?”
“Look. It’s not ‘bout Shinya’s career, alright?”
“I spoke with him, real deep and meaningful-like…”
“He confided in me, but since we’re friends, I s’pose I can share it with yeh.”
“Kotomi Ida has been sexually assaulting him.”
I feign a surprised reaction. In reality, I’m just more taken aback that Shinya actually confessed to Tomoe.
“It’s been goin’ on for months, he says. And now, she’s fucked his career up so he’ll have no choice but to leave the company.”
“He leaves, and she gets off free without anyone findin’ out about what she’s been doin’ to him.”
“I hate her. I hate her so fuckin’ much.”
I try to digest Tomoe’s words. I didn’t know that Shinya has been putting up with the abuse for such a long time.
So, Kotomi’s motive for ending his career was purely out of self-interest.
She was probably looking for a reason—any reason—to discard him. And that slight incident with Aoi was just good enough for her to seize.
If he quits the company, she won’t get found out. It’s a simple plan, but utterly devious.
“We should tell someone what she’s been doing. She can’t get away with that.”
“She ain’t gonna get away with it. Corpse Girl’s comin’ for her, remember?”
“Ah ha ha… I can’t wait to hear the news about Kotomi windin’ up dead somewhere. I hope she gets her throat slit!”
“But, hey… How didja find out about it?”
Tomoe cocks her head and gives me a concerned look. I brace myself as I watch the gears slowly turning inside her head, waiting for her to point the finger at me.
I don’t know why I thought it was a good idea to reveal this information to Tomoe. I should have just kept my mouth shut and fulfilled the request like always.
Damn it…! Why does my curiosity always get the better of me? I’m going to cause my own demise at the rate I’m going.
“Hmm… Oh, I figured it out!”
“Kotomi must’a received a photo and told yeh ‘bout it, huh?”
“Wow! That Corpse Girl sure works fast.”
Tomoe’s gleeful expression suddenly caves in and she gasps.
“Wait a minute! Why would she even show yeh somethin’ like that?”
“When I think ‘bout it, there was that time yeh got a photo, but nothin’ happened to yeh…”
“Then… The only way yeh coulda really known ‘bout Kotomi is…”
I flinch as Tomoe takes a purposeful step toward me.
“Yer Corpse Girl, aren’t yeh?”
“Yeh have to be. It’s the only thing that makes sense.”
I avert my gaze and look to the floor in silence.
“Gawd… Are yeh for real?”
“I can’t believe it…”
“You took your sweet time figuring it out.”
“Don’t give me that bullshit. Yeh can’t expect me to figure out somethin’ like that if yer gonna try so hard to hide it.”
“What the fuck, girl? Yeh get your rocks off by killin’ people?”
“No, not exactly. I don’t kill people.”
“The hell yeh don’t. Explain that bitch Tsurumaki.”
“She killed herself.”
“Yeah, ‘she killed herself.’ That’s the cover-up, right?”
“I’m serious. She killed herself… But Corpse Girl encouraged her to do it.”
Tomoe blinks a few times, her face scrunching up and analyzing my blank expression.
“Yer tellin’ the truth…”
“Holy shit.”
“I can’t believe this. Yer really Corpse Girl?”
There’s no going back now. After hiding my true identity for nearly a year, I’ve managed to reveal it to two people in less than twenty-four hours.
I just hope I haven’t made a fatal mistake.
“It’s true. I’m Corpse Girl.”
“Ah ha ha…!”
“Ha ha ha! Wow, fuck me, right? All this time, I’ve been thinkin’ yer just some goth skank with weird hobbies!”
“But yer actually pretty fuckin’ cool… Yer actually doin’ somethin’ with yer life!”
“Huh…? I… I thought you’d be angry with me…”
“Angry? Why would I be angry? Gawd, this is the coolest thing that’s ever happened to me!”
“I’m friends with fuckin’ Corpse Girl! And people said I’d never amount to nothin’!”
“Though, it took me long enough to figure it out! I ain’t the sharpest lightbulb in the shed.”
“I can’t argue with that.”
Tomoe laughs and puts her arm around my shoulder. I shrink away a little, but her good cheer is somewhat infectious.
I feel a flood of relief wash through my body.
“So, like… I gotta know. How many people have yeh killed?”
“I said I don’t kill people. Remember?”
“Yeah, yeah. Y’know what I mean. How many have offed ‘emselves ‘cos of yeh?”
“It’s an embarrassingly small number.”
“That so? Aww, that’s a shame.”
“Listen, yeh gotta fill me in on all the juicy deets later, ‘kay? For now, please focus on gettin’ rid of that bitch Kotomi.”
“I’ll do my best.”
“Thanks, slut. Shinya ‘n I will owe yeh one, for sure.”
Tomoe swings around and looks toward the elevator. She turns back and gives me a thumbs-up gesture.
“This convo never happened. Got it?”
“That’s my line. You can’t tell anyone about me and Corpse Girl.”
“Please. Who would I tell?”
“Well, the police, for starters…”
“Pssht. Fuck ‘em. I ain’t a squealer.”
“I’m on yer side, Corpse Girl. Relax.”
“Anyway. Peace!”
Tomoe ducks away and leaves me standing alone.
I really hope I made the right decision here…
I suppose I don’t have a choice but to keep moving forward. My first order of business should be to take care of Kotomi Ida.
If I can get her to kill herself, it’ll prove to Tomoe that I’m not messing around. And it might cement our friendship even further.
I just have to get through the rest of the workday. Then, I can return home and focus on crafting Kotomi’s corpse photo.
That’s when the real fun will begin…
I reach into the drawer and clutch a cheap, plastic burner phone between my fingers.
Crafting the photo of Kotomi Ida is done. All I need to do now is send it.
I thought about waiting until tomorrow. But I already put off making the photo for a day. So I’ll make my move tonight.
During editing, I timestamped the photo with tomorrow’s date. 10:46am.
It doesn’t leave much time if Kotomi receives the photo tonight. But I’m confident the plan will be effective.

Kotomi will look at the photo tonight. She’ll either freak out and end it all immediately, or, after a sleepless night of anxiety, she’ll pull the trigger—figuratively speaking—instead of going to the office in the morning.
I could cross my fingers and hope that by divine intervention, someone else will take her life. But, based on my recent failures, I don’t think that’s likely anymore.
If anyone else was ever involved in the deaths of Corpse Girl’s victims, I don’t think they’re still around. Why else would my last few attempts have failed?
No, my best bet is to urge Kotomi to simply kill herself. A convincing-enough corpse photo might be enough to lure her to her death.
When I turn on the burner phone, I’m happy to see the battery is still charged.
I load up the phone number masking app, enter my trademark digits, and then shoot the photo into the network.
If Kotomi is a screen addict like the rest of society, she’ll be freaking out in about ten seconds.
Since this victim is going to have a quick turnaround time, I’ll take the burner to the back shed tonight to store it. And I’ll ditch it on the way to the office tomorrow.
I’m not expecting a reply within such a narrow timeframe. So there’s no need to hold onto the phone for twenty-four hours like I normally do.
Clutching the phone with one hand, I grab my keys from the kitchen bench with the other.
I step toward the front door.
The phone in my hand vibrates violently and I nearly drop it in terror.
“What the…?”
I bring the screen swiftly to my face and read the alert.
‘1 new message.’
Without thinking, I unlock the phone and open the message.
It’s a reply from Kotomi Ida…!
You think this is funny? I know who you are.
I’ll report you to the police.
“Oh my god…”
Holy shit…!
“Ah ha ha…!”
She actually replied! For the first time since Corpse Girl started her grand work, I’ve actually received a reply from a victim!
Even though I use the number mask, there’s actually nothing stopping someone from directly replying to my message.
A reply message would still get sent through the network and back to the burner phone’s sim card.
The number mask is simply a stealth tactic, disabling the ability to view what the phone number actually is. It doesn’t prevent replies.
I discard the burner phones anyway, but it’s an extra layer of security, not to mention a bit of a calling card.
Judging by Kotomi’s response, I assume we have a fighter on our hands. She’s not going to give in easily.
Her threat about reporting me to the police is a bluff. I’m confident that she couldn’t possibly know my identity.
“I’ve been waiting for this…! I’ve waited so long for someone to reply…!”
I can finally put my contingency plan into practice. I’ve been holding out for this moment!
I feel a wicked grin split my face in two and I mash my fingers against the screen as I compose a venomous reply.
You like that photo? That’s you in about 12 hours - unless you follow my instructions.
The message sends in an instant and I eagerly await the next reply.
I’m not left waiting for long. Kotomi’s response comes through within seconds.
Her attitude has completely changed.
Please. I’ll do anything. What do you want?
“Ha ha ha! I called your bluff, you piece of shit!”
“Now you’ll do what I tell you to!”
I enter my instructions, clearly and concisely.
Pack 500,000円 into a bag. Put it in coin locker 6644 at Shinjuku station.
Retrieve the item already inside.
Put the locker key inside a full soda bottle and leave it on top of the locker.
After I send the message, I decide to add one last bit.
Do it now. Make sure no one sees you.
Then go to platform 12. Do not board a train.
Await my instructions.
Satisfied with this addendum, I hit send.
If Kotomi truly fears for her wellbeing, she’ll carry out the instructions.
Her response arrives shortly.
OK. I’ll do it. I’m going there now.
I’ve done it. I’ve convinced her…!
I’ll collect the money once I’m sure she is no longer hanging around.
Five hundred thousand yen is nothing to sneeze at. It’s not life-changing, but it’ll cover my rent for a good few months.
I chose this amount to simply test the waters. Asking for an insane amount would make it impossible for a victim to follow through.
But, I figured someone like Kotomi—an exec for a big company—would easily have access to this much dough.
I’ll go collect the money.
And if everything goes well, Kotomi Ida will disappear before sunrise.
Though the hour is late, quite a few commuters are still navigating through Shinjuku station’s wide platforms and underground labyrinth.
The train station beneath my feet is a sprawling metropolis that extends below the city. It’s packed with restaurants, shops, and other outlets.
But, as I’m standing on one of the countless train platforms above ground, that world might as well be a completely different dimension.
The only problem is that I’ll have to brave the maze as soon as I descend the platform’s stairs.
I tend to get dizzy in such places.
My normal morning route doesn’t require me to travel through the underground plaza. I’m able to exit the station within minutes of my train arriving at the platform.
Still, I’m somewhat familiar with the layout of the underground. I know exactly where coin locker 6644 is located.
The coin lockers in train stations like these are a popular way for people to store luggage or personal belongings for a few hours at a time.
In Shinjuku, it can often be difficult to find even a single available locker.
But coin locker 6644 is special.
I approach it from the main passageway of the underground and my eyes take in the familiar sight.
Locker 6644 sits in the middle row, nestled between countless other lockers.
Across its door is a thick coat of graffiti. Colorful curse words sprayed on with thick paint adorn the locker.
The graffiti is such an eyesore that it acts as a deterrent to anyone who might want to store their belongings.
The icing on the cake is the condition of the coin-operated lock. The thing is busted and dented from physical abuse, like someone has tried to pry into it with a crowbar on multiple occasions.
However, I know from testing it firsthand that the lock still works, despite its battered appearance.
No one in their right mind would use this locker. And that makes it the perfect spot to host my pick up.
Glancing at the locker, I notice that a soda bottle sits on top of it. A soda bottle full of bubbly opaque liquid.
I quickly look around to make sure that Kotomi Ida is nowhere in sight. I walk past the locker and complete a lap around the immediate area, scanning thoroughly for her.
But she isn’t here. In fact, there are very few people in this little section of the station.
Good. She followed my instructions perfectly. After leaving the key in the soda bottle, she left immediately.
I approach the locker once more. I reach up above it and retrieve the soda bottle, then crack it open to hear the fizzy hiss.
I bring the lip of the bottle to eye level and peer inside, trying to identify the shape of a key within the swirling ocean of carbonation.
There it is…!
I try to fish inside the narrow bottle opening with my fingers. Thin though they are, I can’t squeeze more than one finger inside the bottle at a time.
I could tip the bottle over and let the soda—and the key—spill out onto the floor. But if someone sees me being a nuisance and causing a mess, it’ll draw unwanted attention.
I’ve got no choice but to chug back some of the soda and try to catch the key in my mouth.
As disgusting as the concept is, I need to steel myself.
I raise the bottle to my lips, tilt my head back, and pour the foul liquid into my open mouth.
The saccharine tang of artificial flavoring assaults my tastebuds and I immediately want to vomit.
But I’m committed to seeing this through. I can throw up later. The most important thing is getting the key.
It isn’t until the bottle is half empty that the cold metal key drops into my mouth. It clangs against my teeth and I nearly choke in surprise.
Sputtering and spitting, I feel droplets of soda running down my chin. My cheeks are puffed up like a squirrel as I try to retain the key and the soda in my mouth.
I reach my fingers into pursed, tight lips, and recover the tiny key. I quickly swallow down the rest of the soda in my mouth, trying hard not to release a repugnant belch.
I turn the key over in my hand and smile. My sticky teeth adhere to my lips and it takes me a few seconds to lick them clean.
Tossing the soda bottle into the nearby trash can, I wipe the key clean on my skirt and quickly insert it into the coin locker.
I twist the key, turn the latch, and swing the locker door open.
Inside the dark vault is a single bag, a simple paper pouch like you would get at a grocery store.
I pull the paper bag out and take a look inside.
Thick stacks of ten-thousand yen bills fill the bag. I’m not foolish enough to stand here and count it out, but I’m confident the amount is at least pretty close to what I requested.
“It worked… My plan worked…!”
I can hardly believe it.
I devised this contingency plan months ago. I waited so long to try it out.
All I needed was somebody to reply to their corpse photo—somebody to try and reject their fate.
I wanted to prove that people would bow to fear and do anything to save their own skin. And it seems that I was right.
“Just one more thing to do…”
I fold up the paper bag and clutch it tightly. With my free hand, I pull the burner phone out of my handbag.
I compose a message to Kotomi Ida, who should be obediently waiting aboveground on the train platform.
When the next train arrives on your platform, stab the first person to disembark.
You must kill them.
If you escape, leave this prefecture and never return.
It’s done.
When I first opened the coin locker and retrieved the paper bag, I immediately noticed the knife that I had placed inside months ago was missing.
Kotomi followed every word of my instructions.
My message had read, ‘Pack 500,000円 into a bag. Put it in coin locker 6644 at Shinjuku station. Retrieve the item already inside…’
I’ve given Kotomi an opportunity. She can trade another’s life for her own.
If she kills someone exiting the train, Corpse Girl will spare her life.
It’s a simple exchange… and one that I bet she is willing to make.
If she gets away with the murder, she’ll flee from this place. I won’t see her ever again—and neither will Shinya or Tomoe. To us, she’ll be as good as dead.
And as for Corpse Girl, well… As long as a body is claimed in exchange, she’ll be satisfied.
After a few minutes of waiting for a reply to the message, I figure that she’s not going to write back. She’s probably getting ready to fulfill her task.
Keen to witness how this unfolds, I take the nearest escalator up toward the train platform.
The scene is absolute chaos.
It wasn’t difficult at all to navigate to this area. All I had to do was follow the echoing screams.
I spy the shadowed form of a body lying on the platform in front of me. I can’t make out any details, but a shallow pool of blood reflects the harsh lights shining from up high.
To my surprise—and delight—a second body is sprawled across the ground nearby.
It’s a young woman’s corpse, with one arm raised against the side of a vending machine.
Adrenaline surges through me at the violent scene. Kotomi Ida… She managed to take out two people! She might be my new favorite person in the entire world.
I hear panicked voices in the background, and I turn my head slowly.
What the…?
Two more bodies are on the ground!
Two men in expensive-looking suits are collapsed in puddles of their own lifeblood. One of the men is still moving and groaning, pleading for somebody to stem the tide of gore.
A familiar, lustful tingling sensation begins to stir and rise through my belly, my thighs, my pelvis… I feel my toes clench and my breathing grows heavier.
There’s one more surprise to be had here amidst this beautiful spectacle of carnage.
A woman is slumped in one of the plastic chairs that lines the platform. Her head is tilted, her suit jacket stained with red.
A thick knife with a black grip protrudes from the side of her neck. A bubbling river of vital fluid cascades around the glimmering blade and pools within her shirt collar.
Even with her face masked by blood, it doesn’t take me more than a few seconds to recognize her identity.
Kotomi Ida.
I swing around and take in the entire view of the platform. Counting up the bodies and the path of slaughter, my mind pieces together a theoretical scenario.
Kotomi waited as the train doors opened, knife drawn—the knife she retrieved from locker 6644.

When the first person stepped out of the train, she stabbed him and left him for dead. The body that I first saw, laying on the edge of the platform, is perfectly aligned next to the train to fit this theory.
In a panic, Kotomi would have attempted to flee. She bumped into her second victim, the young woman slumped against the vending machine, and cut her down desperately to make her escape.

Judging by the wound on Kotomi’s own body, I would assume the two businessmen lying face down tried to apprehend her. They must have sustained fatal wounds before finally managing to wrest the knife away and plunge it into Kotomi’s neck.
It’s all just speculation, but I’m fairly confident that’s how this whole event played out. It was probably over in less than sixty seconds.
And it couldn’t have worked out better for me.
I never dared hope that Kotomi would meet her end once this plan had been set into motion. I would have been satisfied with her simply skipping town.
I feel my legs weakening under my weight and I’m afraid I might buckle at any second. The waves of radiating heat spreading through my body are causing me to tremble and shake.
There’s so much blood. It’s everywhere.
I’ve seen it in countless photos and thought I had become desensitized to it…
But maybe I was wrong. Seeing blood in real life is completely different. I feel faint and pale and excited and aroused.
I need to get out of here before the police arrive. More importantly, I need to get away before I collapse in a sweaty heap of lust and pleasure.
I turn on my heel and sprint down the rising escalator as fast as my quivering legs will permit.
