“A bizarre string of similar deaths in Tokyo over the weekend have left police and detectives completely baffled.”
“We have Chief Detective Fujikawa of the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department in the studio today to discuss the events.”
“According to eyewitness reports, a young woman plummeted to her death from an apartment building on Saturday morning.”
“Two other women suffered a similar fate, in different locations, late on Sunday night.”
“Police have not yet released information on the identities of the young women. Would you care to share your thoughts, Detective Fujikawa?”
“We cannot rule out the possibility of homicide in these cases.”
“Police recovered additional bodies at the site of each death. In each instance, a look-alike corpse, matching the appearance of the victim, was found.”
“This can not be mere coincidence. I believe that a single perpetrator is behind the deaths of all three women.”
“Leaving a look-alike corpse at the scene of each crime seems to be some sort of psychotic calling card. It’s clear that the death of each victim was premeditated.”
“In cases like these, the perpetrator is often looking to be caught—even if only subconsciously.”
“It won’t take long to track them down. Once forensic analysis reveals the identities of the look-alike corpses, we will be able to uncover how and where they were obtained.”
“We will bring the perpetrator to justice.”
“Police are urging citizens to be cautious in the coming weeks. If you see anyone behaving suspiciously, please call the following number…”
“Daaaaamn. This shit’s really startin’ to blow up.”
“Yeah. It’s about time.”
“Three deaths in one weekend. Corpse Girl is on fire!”
“She couldn’t have done it without you. And Kojiro.”
“So, thanks. I know those corpse deliveries yesterday were rather last-minute.”
“No problem. Had nothin’ better to do, anyway.”
“I’ve still got one victim ready to conquer, but…”
“I’m not sure when to go through with it.”
“What’s the issue?”
“It’s… It’s someone I know.”
“Eh? So? Didn’t bother yeh when we stuck it to that Emi chick.”
“This is a little different.”
“It’s my sister…”
“Yo! Hold up. Yeh’ve got a sister?”
“Yuriko. She’s older than me.”
“Shiiiiit. And, like, someone requested her death through Corpse Girl’s website?”
“Seems like it.”
“Geez. What’re the chances?”
“I’m wondering the same thing.”
“Well, think it over a bit longer. Yeh might wanna lay low for a while, anyway.”
“Sounds like Shinya’s dad is all over this case…”
“Sorry? Shinya’s dad?”
“That detective guy. Fujikawa.”
“What…? He’s Shinya’s dad?”
“Yup. Friggin’ scary guy. Had an awkward dinner with him ‘n Shinya a while back.”
“You know, I met him once before…”
“Yeh did?”
“He certainly was intimidating. But don’t worry. We only met by chance. Had nothing to do with Corpse Girl.”
“All right. As long as he doesn’t know yer identity, yeh should be fine.”
“Still… What’s yer next move?”
“I’ll think over what to do about my sister for a little longer.”
“But as soon as more requests come through the website, I’m going to fulfill them.
“I don’t have the luxury of time. I can’t just ‘lay low,’ like you said.”
“Sheesh. When did yeh grow a pair?”
“I’m serious. I’m tired of lagging behind.”
“Corpse Girl is on a winning streak now. It’s up to me to keep it going.”
“Okay, okay. Well, just let me know when yeh need me.”
“Thanks. I will.”
“Well, back to work. Or whatever. Ah ha ha!”
I turn back to my computer after Tomoe leaves.
Three deaths in one weekend…
Corpse Girl truly is at the top of her game.
It was a bit of hard work, but in the end, I managed to pull through. Thanks to a bit of luck, of course.
Yesterday, after returning home from the library, I had a sudden burst of inspiration.
I ran a reverse image search on the photos of the two women that were submitted to Corpse Girl’s website. It was pretty easy to locate their noise profiles thanks to that.
I was kind of shocked when I saw that we all shared two mutual friends on noise: Emi Katsuno and Yuriko Kurosawa.
A bit of digging through their profiles revealed their names to be Fuyumi Amano and Manami Sachiko. They both worked at the same store as Emi… And my sister.
It struck me then that all of these requests must be somehow related. But that didn’t matter so much.
Tracking down Amano’s and Sachiko’s addresses wasn’t as difficult as I’d feared. I contacted Tomoe, and she told me she was familiar with the store they worked at.
She volunteered to head over there and see if she could access the employee records.

Apparently, the whole job was so easy that she managed to walk in and out in three minutes flat. She said that none of the staff even batted an eyelid as she walked in, and she simply strode into the back room, rummaged through the filing cabinet, and snapped a photo of the employee contact sheet.
With that information at our disposal, nothing stood in our way of delivering look-alike corpses to their homes.
A few hours shared between the morgue and the factory, and…
It was done.
Both Amano and Sachiko killed themselves within an hour of each other.
So far, the kill rate of delivering a photo and then a corpse is one hundred percent.
I can only imagine the thoughts that must go through someone’s mind when they are faced with their own corpse.
The looming dread, hopelessness, and fear of inevitability have proven to be so overwhelming that suicide becomes the only viable option.
Because of this development, I’ve finally ruled out the possibility of Corpse Girl’s victims being murdered by some mysterious stranger.

I only ever invented that theory due to the strange circumstances in which Ruri Hatano died. After all, she was hung from a scarecrow in an uncannily similar fashion to the corpse photo I invented for her.

None of the other victim’s deaths since then have made me truly suspect that another party could be involved. All of them have clearly been suicides, or in the case of Eiichi Hanada, coincidental accidents.
Kotomi Ida’s death was an outlier since she was likely killed out of self-defense.
I’m about ninety percent certain that Corpse Girl’s power lies in the ability to convince victims to end their own lives. There’s no third-party murderer acting on her behalf.
And I’ve begun to suspect that the power I hold is no esoteric, arcane force. It’s not some supernatural art. It’s not witchcraft, or sorcery, or some holy power bestowed upon me from on high.
The power Corpse Girl holds is simple determination. Grit. Resolve.
My will to end lives is what drives me to craft convincing corpse photos and deliver look-alike cadavers.
That in itself is enough to act as the knife twisting in a victim’s side. It’s enough to compel those weak of heart and weak of mind to end their lives.
If that’s all my power ends up being, I am happy. I am happy that I can be the instrument that delivers Corpse Girl’s justice, regardless of whether it’s through mundane or mysterious methods.
As long as victims continue to drop like flies in the wake of Corpse Girl’s ascension, I will remain content.
And this is only just the beginning.
There are no new requests when I log in to Corpse Girl’s website this evening.
I’m strangely okay with that. There’s something I want to do before more requests come through, anyway.
I’m going to make some updates to the website. A few improvements that will considerably ease the workload placed upon Corpse Girl, Kojiro, and Tomoe.
In the website’s admin settings, I add a couple of extra data fields to the front page.
Instead of just asking for a photo and a phone number, the website now requires a victim’s address to be provided. This will ensure we can successfully deliver a corpse for every request.
In addition… The site now asks for the victim’s name.
I have always been hesitant about requesting this specific detail.
I never wanted to know the names of the people Corpse Girl will kill. It creates familiarity, and I always used to worry that it would prevent me from going through with a request.
But, more than all of that…
I feared that I would delve too deep into somebody’s life. I feared that I would become too attached, too entranced by standing on the outside and looking in.
Knowing someone’s name would have allowed me to easily find victims online and go down the rabbit hole of spying on their private lives.
My voyeuristic fetishes would have defeated me. I know myself, and I know that I would have become far too interested in a person to carry out their death.
It’s the same reason why I never reverse image searched a victim’s photo before yesterday.
Now that things are escalating… Now that Corpse Girl needs a victim’s address to ensure a kill…
I have to get past all of that. I have to be strong for Corpse Girl.

I’m somewhat relieved that the timing is suitable. After all, I haven’t been as aroused as usual when stalking people online. I don’t know if my libido is just low, or if I truly have become uninterested in such things…
Either way, I believe I’m able to cope with the burden of extra knowledge. Learning victim’s names, addresses, all of that… It’s going to work in Corpse Girl’s favor.
And I’m surely strong enough now to not give in to temptation and succumb to the scopophilia that has plagued my existence for years.
After adding the victim’s name and address fields to the website, I decide to add one final touch.
There’s a particular line of text that describes how the site works. I’ve always liked it.
It says, ‘Your victim will receive a photo of their own corpse shortly before they die.’
It’s concise, and it perfectly sums up the intention of the website.
However, it needs to be updated to correctly apply to Corpse Girl’s new modus operandi.
I change the line, ever so slightly. Just enough to make a difference.
It now reads, ‘Your victim will receive their own corpse shortly before they die.’
Some people might think it doesn’t make sense. They’ll think that maybe it’s a typo, or written by someone not familiar with the language.
But it is completely intentional.
Now that I’ve made all the changes to the website, I click the ‘save’ button in the admin panel.
The changes are reflected immediately on the front page of the site.
Corpse Girl’s new and improved request form is online.
With that done, I need to simply sit back and wait for some new requests to pour in.
And it shouldn’t take long once I put my next plan into motion.
Because I’ve finally figured out how my sister can be of use to me after all these years.
She’s going to help me become famous.
Yuriko Kurosawa’s death will ensure that everybody in Japan knows the name ‘Corpse Girl.’
Text_Month="June 16";Text_Day="TUESDAY";Text_Time="Morning"
For the first time in a while, my fingers scrape against the bottom of the cabinet drawer.
“Oh, shit…”
I fumble around and grab the last remaining burner phone in the drawer. It’s a fairly modern handset from around three years ago.
These newer models never retain their battery charge for more than a month or so when they’ve been inactive.
Thankfully, it uses a generic charger, so I quickly plug it into the kitchen outlet and wait for it to return to life.
I glance back down at the open drawer. It’s completely empty now. I’m going to need to restock my supply of burners if I hope to continue with Corpse Girl’s work.
I nervously bite my fingernails at the thought.
Getting these phones isn’t easy. It’s free, yes, but not easy.
And if I get busted trying to lift a stack of them, that might very well be the end of me.
I’ll have to obtain as many new phones as possible at some point today. Once Corpse Girl kills my sister, my website is going to explode with new requests.
I need to be as prepared as possible.
I decide to finish getting ready for work while the burner charges.
As much as I’d like to simply skip out and deal with my sister, I do need to pop into the office.
Missing too many days is going to lead to getting fired and that might compromise my mission.
I take my medication. I apply my makeup. I pack my handbag.
It’s all so mundane, but it’s all so necessary. Each day is the same routine. There’s comfort to be found in that, especially for someone like me, but…
Sometimes I remember the excitement of finding myself in new situations.
Even if those situations end up with me lying in the muck of a bathroom floor, or against the stone-cold tiles of a morgue…
When I’m ready to leave the apartment, I snatch the burner phone up and check the battery. It’s at around forty percent. That should be plenty.
I stash it in my handbag so it’s ready for action when the time comes.
I’m out the door at the same time as every other day.
I find myself alone in the office well after the working day has ended.
The entire floor is empty and silent.
I shut down my computer and stretch my tense arms.
I don’t normally like staying back late, but sometimes it’s necessary to get work done. And when I say ‘work,’ I am of course referring to Corpse Girl’s tasks.
When I’m absolutely certain that everybody has gone home, I get out of my chair and wander listlessly around the office.
It’s kind of nice having the place to myself. It’s like my apartment, only bigger, and colder, and without that terrible odor of mold that permeates the walls.

I notice that quite a few people tend to leave their belongings at their desks. Nothing too valuable—the occasional coat, hat, or pair of headphones. Should somebody of low moral character wish to steal them, there would be nothing stopping them…
I’m personally not interested in any of that.
I walk to the other side of the office floor and reach the seniors’ cubicles.
Even the seniors leave important things lying around. There’s a gift bag with a cake shop logo on the front, a company credit card, a few personal bank statements…
But the contents of their desk drawers are where the real gold is found.
As I rifle through one drawer in particular, I find exactly what I’m looking for.
It’s an old noise-brand phone, a few models earlier than my own.
It slips into my handbag, right alongside the burner phone I brought from home. I close the desk drawer gently and traipse into the next cubicle.
The top drawer here contains a flip phone, a familiar classic. It’ll serve me well. Into the handbag it goes.
One of the main problems I have with this company—with any company, in fact—is the wasteful attitude of management.

Executives, seniors, and even some junior staff are provided with company phones. Basically, if you’re expected to make calls on the job, the company will issue you a phone so that you don’t have to use your own.

However… With the rapid evolution of modern technology, phones often find themselves replaced or upgraded well before they cease functioning. And management doesn’t care about recycling or repurposing unused, obsolete phones.
The devices simply drift to the bottom of drawers or storage cabinets, destined to become forgotten within moments.
Am I really doing the wrong thing by taking these phones off the company’s hands? It’s not like I’m stealing personal property from employees.
I’m only taking what the company is likely to write-off as a business expense. And this is a multi-billion yen company—are they really going to miss the odd outdated device?
I justified this to myself long ago. I’m ensuring these phones are used for a bigger purpose. And there’s nothing bigger than fulfilling Corpse Girl’s ambitions.
As I swipe the fourth or fifth phone, I hear the ‘ding’ of the elevator from across the office floor.
Someone’s here. I need to get away from the cubicles without being seen…
“Noriko? Is that you?”
I must have ducked down a second too late because the voice identified me correctly.
I scuttle forward on my knees, just a little bit, so that I’m not so close to the cubicles.
When I get to my feet, I’m halfway between the senior employee’s area and the juniors’ open-plan desks.
Shinya walks over from the elevator to greet me.
“Hi. You’re here awfully late.”
“Er… What were you doing over there? That is, if you don’t mind me asking.”
“I lent my USB drive to one of the seniors earlier, and they didn’t return it, so…”
“Oh. Did you find it?”
“Nope. Oh well. I’ll ask about it tomorrow.”
“I could help you look, if you like.”
“Seriously, it’s okay. I’m about to head home, anyway.”
“What are you doing here?”
“I left my wallet at my desk. Can you believe it?”
“Luckily, I remembered before I took Tomoe out for dinner!”
“I would have appeared to be quite the buffoon if I had been unable to pay for our meal. Ha ha ha!”
“Er… Yeah, I suppose so.”
“Hey… How are things, anyway?”
“Things with Tomoe are great! We are truly in love.”
“Wow. Okay. Not exactly, what I meant, but…”
“How are things here? I mean, what happened with Kotomi, and…”
“Ah. That whole kerfuffle.”
“Can you believe Ms. Ida is dead now?”
“Is… Is it wrong of me to say that I’m happy she’s dead?”
“Is that an awful thing to admit?”
I gently shake my head, but I don’t interrupt his train of thought.
“It’s so bizarre... Especially considering our relationship, and how determined she was to end my career...”
It bothers me that Shinya is still referring to the conflict between himself and Kotomi as a ‘relationship.’
“But, it would seem that she was the only one with animosity toward me.”
“As such, the other executives said I am welcome to work here as long as I like.”
“In fact, they were even generous enough to give me a small salary raise!”
“Wow! That’s great, Shinya. I’m really happy for you.”
“Thank you!”
“It truly was a struggle there, for a little while…”
Before my brain can even register what I’m saying, the following words tumble out of my mouth.
“Do you want to talk about it?”
“Noriko… I know that I haven’t been as open with you as I should have been.”
“Maybe talking about it will help me put the whole thing behind me.”
I bite my tongue as I try to think of a way to back out of the situation.
“Oh… Um, you know, if you’re uncomfortable talking to me, maybe Tomoe can help…”
My objection is met with a smile. Looks like I’m in too deep now.
“Tomoe means well. She really does. But whenever I bring up the subject, she becomes visibly angry.”
“Many a death threat against Ms. Ida has been made aloud.”
“I wouldn’t be all too surprised if Tomoe was the one who killed her. Ha ha. There certainly is a motive there, after all.”
“Hmm… So, you don’t know who killed Kotomi...?”
“I don’t think even the police know that much. Father showed me the photos of the crime scene.”
“Chances are that whoever did kill her was also killed in return.”
“Though… As abusive as she was toward me, I never took her as the type to instigate a mass murder.”
“She was an angry person, yes… But that seemed to stem from a lack of... fulfillment. That’s what I assume, anyway.”
“And I think that’s the reason she made her advances on me.”
“I really am sorry. I’m so sorry that you had to go through such a traumatic experience.”
“I thought I was going to lose everything.”
“My job, my relationship…”
“Ms. Ida threatened to steal it all away from me… Just so she could experience some form of power, some small manner of pleasure…”
“Why do people do those things, Noriko?”
“What joy is there even to be found in… In…”
I take my time to consider my reply.
I’m probably not the best person for him to be having this discussion with, but… All things considered, it does seem to be helping him come to terms with things.
“What you went through with Kotomi… What she did to you… That’s not what it’s about. She never had the right to put you through that.”
“I hope that one day, when you’re comfortable, and feeling healthy…”
“I hope that you can make some good memories with Tomoe.”
“Yes… I hope so.”
“Thank you, Noriko.”
“Don’t mention it.”
I don’t know if my words were the right ones. What right do I have to talk about what he went through?
I can only hope that I managed to bring him some sort of comfort.
“Well, I’d better grab my wallet and get going. Don’t want to keep Tomoe waiting!”
“Say… Would you like to join us, Noriko?”
“Are you hungry at all?”
“Oh… I don’t want to intrude on your romantic evening.”
“It’s no trouble! Really!”
“Um… Maybe next time. I have some things I need to do tonight.”
“Okay. No problem.”
“Well, see you later!”
Shinya takes off toward his desk. I breathe a sigh of relief as I hoist my handbag up from the ground, feeling the reassuring weight of my newly acquired burner phones.
I enter the elevator and give a polite wave to Shinya as the doors close.
“Give me a call back when you leave the restaurant.”
“Ugh. Yeh want me to drive tonight?”
“It has to be tonight. We talked about this.”
“Please. Kojiro is on standby as well.”
“Pssht! Fine.”
“Not like I’ve been dyin’ to bring Shinya back to my place or nothin’...”
“Don’t push Shinya. Let him tell you when he’s ready.”
“Yeah, yeah, I know.”
“Look, I’ll prolly be outta the restaurant in an hour. That cool?”
“Yes. Thanks.”
Tomoe hangs up.
I look down the street, my gaze aiming directly at the restaurant Tomoe is currently seated at with Shinya.
I’ll need to kill an hour around here. But what is there to do?
I’m not exactly keen on the idea of window-shopping. I don’t even want to be here. But standing in one spot as dozens of people walk by is really nerve-wracking.
I could go visit Aoi at the maid cafe… But, then I’d have to pay the table charge to enter, and it’d probably be pretty weird to be served by girls in maid costumes. Not really my thing.
As I glance around, I notice a twenty-four-hour manga cafe at the end of the street.
That could actually be perfect… I could rent a quiet space for a few hundred yen and just read a book until it’s time to go. No one there to bother me.
In fact, the only person I’d need to speak to is the attendant at the counter.
With my mind made up, I hurry along to the manga cafe.
“Pretty late.”
“Come on. You’re a night owl. What are you complaining about?”
“Just making chit-chat.”
“Well, instead of talking, how about you hold that flashlight still?”
“I can’t see what I’m doing with you waving it around.”
“Yes, ma’am.”
“I’m nearly done, anyway.”
“Fucking Yuriko… This wouldn’t be so difficult if she didn’t have different haircuts in every single photo on her profile.”
“I’m just going to have to estimate the length of her hair for now…”
The corpse on the table in front of me looks like an uncanny clone of my sister.
I snip away a little more hair from her fringe and then put the scissors aside.
“You two must be close.”
“The opposite.”
“Makeup’s done!”
“Thanks. Looks good.”
Tomoe beams as she puts the cap back on the lipstick in her hand.
“I think we’re done.”
“Can you zip up the bag? I really need to wash my hands.”
“You got it, boss.”
I step away from the corpse and plunge my hands into the ice-cold bucket of water on the factory floor.
I have to admit that we’ve become pretty good at this whole thing. In just a week or so, we’ve managed to refine our art and synchronize our duties.
“Okay. Load her in the van. I’m going to send the corpse photo now.”
“Yeh sure ‘bout this? Yeh think she’s gonna be awake this time of night?”
“I’m positive. This is the best time to do it.”
According to her noise feed, Yuriko Kurosawa is currently attending a massive party. I’m sure the venue will be packed to the brim with her scumbag friends.
She’s been posting about it for days. It wasn’t hard for me to find out all the information I needed, since whoever organized the party posted it as a public event.
Yuriko is about to receive a photo of her own corpse.
And, in less than an hour’s time, she’s going to receive her carbon-copy corpse in a body bag, in front of at least a hundred people.
The mass panic that will break out is sure to be hilarious. I don’t want to miss it. And I don’t want to miss my sister’s final moments.
Maybe she’ll kill herself in front of her closest friends. Or, maybe the terror will slowly eat away at her, and she’ll go home first before deciding she just can’t take it anymore.
I’m happy with either result.
She’s finally going to get what she deserves. I hate her so much. She’s a low-life degenerate, a delinquent, the utter scum of the earth.
And she never calls me.
I doubt she remembers I even exist.
“Ready to go?”
I snap out of my thoughts and look at the phone that I’ve been subconsciously holding in my feeble grip.
It’s the burner I picked up from home earlier this morning. Yuriko’s corpse photo is glowing on the screen, ready to be launched into the network.
I hit ‘send.’
Kojiro nods and hauls the zipped-up body bag onto his shoulder.
The weight of the cadaver inside causes him to stumble a little, but he regains his balance and shuffles toward the factory entrance.
I examine the body bag as Kojiro carries it.
It’s the same white HRP that we picked up from the morgue. But I’ve made a rather nice adjustment to it.
Big bold letters are scrawled along the sides in purple and black permanent marker.
It says, ‘WITH LOVE FROM CORPSE GIRL!’
Underneath the massive letters, in smaller script, is Corpse Girl’s website address.
A scribble of a cute anime girl decorates the other side of the bag. It’s the very same character that dances animatedly on Corpse Girl’s website.
Tomoe told me this was a bold move. Kojiro didn’t seem to care.
Yuriko Kurosawa is about to be publicly executed. Tonight is the night that Corpse Girl becomes known to the world.
This is the quietest house party I have ever witnessed.
I only manage to catch a glimpse of it before Kojiro shields my eyes with his ice-cold hand.
I want to object to him censoring my vision, but the smell of blood causes me to slump against his shoulder and I resort to whimpering quietly as he places me gently on the ground.
The vision of the house party from hell is still vivid behind my closed eyelids.
It’s not like I’ve been to many house parties in my life. In fact, when I really think about it, I don’t think I’ve ever been to a single one before this moment.
But I’ve seen them on television. I’ve seen them in movies.
They’re always loud. Music is blasting, people are dancing, drinking, making out…
The scene I witnessed doesn’t look like any of that.
I’m pretty sure dead bodies don’t line the floor at a regular house party.
I’m pretty sure trails of blood aren’t on the guest list.
This party is weird.
The walls are slashed. There’s broken glass everywhere. Specks of blood are dotted across the furniture.
Someone in the next room is sobbing quietly. Someone above, perhaps inside the ceiling, is groaning.
Kojiro is sitting next to me now. I can imagine a bored expression hovering over his features.
He still has his hand over my eyes.
He taps the fingers of his other hand against the body bag beside him. His digits drum out a rhythmic beat upon Yuriko Kurosawa’s clone, still zipped up and sealed inside her temporary coffin.
I think Tomoe is still in the van. She said something about ‘not wanting to get messed up.’
I never planned on entering this party. But Kojiro dragged the body inside, then returned shortly after and told me I should come take a look.
So here I am. Here I am, blinded by Kojiro’s misguided attempt to protect me from the carnage I willingly unleashed.
I asked him if he killed all the people here. He said no. I suppose I believe him.
I manage to squint through a gap in Kojiro’s fingers momentarily. The blurred shapes of four or five bodies are on the floor in front of us.
There’s a stray arm lying limply on a chair that’s currently unaccounted for.
Kojiro presses down firmly against my face and my vision darkens once more.
I hear his voice and imagine his calm demeanor in my mind.
“Don’t know.”
I haven’t managed to sort my head out just yet.
“Your sister is over there.”
“Well. A corpse that looks like her, at any rate.”
“Give me a second.”
Kojiro releases his grip from my face.
I stand. I tiptoe forward, stumbling thanks to my still blurry eyes.
I can make out the shape of a sofa close to the wall, and I approach it carefully.
The empty gap between the sofa and the wall is a three-foot-wide space. I’m not sure why the owner of this house doesn’t keep the sofa directly against the wall.
The empty space here seems kind of useless.
Maybe if the sofa is all the way against the wall it becomes too far from the TV. That’s a possibility.
I would personally just get a bigger TV so that the sofa can be kept comfortably flush with the wall.
The gap here really annoys me. It’s making me irritated.
I want to push the sofa back myself, but I know I don’t have the strength.
It’s a massive thing, bigger than I am, and maybe even bigger than Corpse Girl.
Even if I was strong enough to move it, there’s still the issue of my sister lying here between the sofa and the wall.
She’s in the way. I’d have to move her first, and the thought of touching her is absolutely disgusting.
Even when she was alive I never wanted to touch her. She’s a foul excuse for a human being.
“Hey, Yuriko. Long time, no see.”
She doesn’t respond.
“You don’t look so hot.”
“Guess I’m prettier now, huh?”
“Why do you never call me?”
“Whatever. I wouldn’t answer the phone anyway.”
She doesn’t say anything.
The sound of someone grunting behind me doesn’t interrupt my concentration. I assume it’s just Kojiro clearing his throat.
“Have you seen Mother lately?”
“I haven’t heard from her in a while.”
“I’m sure she’s fine.”
“Are you still on parole?”
“I heard you were working at a clothing store.”
“Yeah, I’m fine.”
“I’m working for Temujin at the moment.”
Yuriko nods.
“It’s okay. There are worse jobs, I’m sure.”
“How did you get that cut across your throat?”
“Does it hurt?”
I reach forward and slip my fingers into Yuriko’s gashed throat.
When I remove them, I frown at the red blood dripping down into the gaps between my knuckles.
“That’s disgusting.”
“Remember when you bandaged me up after I busted my knee?”
“You said Mother would be mad if she found out that you hurt me. So you tried your best to fix me up before she got home.”
“She found out, though. I think she’s going to find out about this, too. There’s no way you can keep this from her, Yu-Yu.”
Yuriko smiles gently.
I wipe the blood onto my skirt.
“Oh? Him? That’s Kojiro. He’s a friend.”
“No. There’s nothing between us.”
I hear the grunt from behind once more.
“I know.”
“You’re actually nicer than I remember.”
“Why couldn’t you ever be this nice when we were kids?”
“If you’d been this nice to me, then…”
“Maybe I wouldn’t have spent my entire teenage life wishing you would drop dead.”
“Oh! I guess my wishes came true, after all. Ha ha ha!”
Yuriko laughs along with me. It doesn’t sound like the laugh I remember. It’s more like a gurgle, like she has something caught in her throat.
A trickle of blood pours from between her lips and she coughs.
“Do you need a tissue?”
I unzip my handbag and retrieve a tissue, then hand it to Yuriko. She tilts her head and sprays the rest of the blood from her mouth.
“Fuck… you… Noriko…!”
“I gotta go. Say hi to Father for me, okay?”
I leave Yuriko behind.
After making my way out of the cursed house, I find Kojiro waiting by the van. Tomoe has shut herself inside and rolled up all the windows.
“I think we’re done here.”
“Leave this here?”
He lazily indicates the body bag on the ground.
“Yeah. I guess so. We didn’t need it after all.”
“Guess not.”
Kojiro slaps his broad hands across his trousers, dusting them off. He cocks his neck to the side and stretches his limbs.
I make an attempt to reach for the van’s door, but Kojiro stops me.
“Not curious about what happened?”
“Only a little. She’s dead, though. Or dying. That’s all that matters.”
“Oh! Actually. Give me one second!”
I quickly dart back inside the house.
I weave across the room and duck behind the sofa once more. Yuriko is silent and unmoving.
I do my best to push her body to the side with my skeletal arms. She budges an inch or two, and I find what I’m looking for—her phone buried between her ass and the carpet.
I turn on the screen and find there’s no fingerprint or passcode lock.
The photo of Yuriko’s corpse—the very same photo that I sent to her earlier—is still on the screen.
“I guess she did receive the photo, then.”
“Maybe that’s all it took this time.”
“She must have been pretty freaked if she killed all the people here… This is like the Kotomi Ida situation all over again.”
My voyeuristic tendencies flare up and I decide to look through the rest of her photos.
I swipe across the screen just once and nearly jump out of my skin.
Yuriko received a photo right before she received the one I sent. It arrived ten minutes before my photo.
It’s another image of a corpse.
Another photo depicting her death—but it’s completely different than the one I crafted.
“What the fuck…?”
Someone else sent Yuriko Kurosawa a photo of her own corpse only ten minutes before I did.
Yuriko received a corpse photo from somebody else…
What is going on…?
I examine the photo in detail. It’s well-made, just like my own work. If I didn’t know any better, it would be easy to assume that I made this.
But what stands out the most is the writing on the bottom of the image.
It simply says, ‘Stab Shuji at the party.’
Stab Shuji at the party…
Who the hell is Shuji? Is he here? Is he one of the dead bodies scattered around this accursed house?
I quickly discard the thoughts of Shuji. A more important question has come to my attention.
Is someone else crafting corpse photos and sending them to people…?
Does Corpse Girl have a copycat…? An imitator…?
But why target Yuriko…? Why target somebody whose death was requested through Corpse Girl’s website?
I can’t process this right now. It’s already past midnight and I’m utterly exhausted.
I shove Yuriko’s phone into my handbag and get the hell out of the house.
Text_Month="June 17";Text_Day="WEDNESDAY";Text_Time="Morning"
Today is not a suitable day to go to the office.
Today is not a suitable day to wake up and shower.
Today is not a suitable day to force those tiny pills down my throat.
Today is a day to lay in bed and rest my face on the pillow caked with yesterday’s makeup.
I don’t know what the time is. I don’t really care.
My phone has buzzed several times, but I simply don’t have the energy to reach over and look at it.
I want to just stay here and be warm and comfortable and not think about anything.
I don’t want to think about that house party last night, but I keep thinking about it.
I don’t want to think about finding Yuriko’s body in that irritating, useless space between the sofa and the wall.
I don’t want to think about my sister’s final words to me. Those bitter syllables that she used all of her remaining strength to force between her blood-soaked lips.
I don’t want to think about the fact that I’d probably have said the same thing to her if I was in her position.
I don’t want to think about the possibility that someone else was responsible for Yuriko’s death.
It was supposed to be Corpse Girl—me! Me! Me! Me!
I was supposed to be responsible for my sister’s death!
Somebody else caused her death...
How dare they steal that from me…? How dare they!?
A copycat… A nobody…
The more that I don’t think about it, the more I find myself thinking about it.
Think, think, think… Why would somebody copy Corpse Girl’s methods…?
How would somebody copy Corpse Girl’s methods?
Corpse Girl is mine! MINE!
Corpse Girl belongs to me!
I’m not infamous enough yet to have an imposter. Surely. I’d be kidding myself with delusions of grandeur to think that I’ve earned an imitator.
But… The fact remains that somebody sent Yuriko a corpse photo. A corpse photo that was meticulously edited and just as convincing as anything I could make.
And those instructions…
Stab Shuji at the party.
Stab. Shuji.
Did Yuriko do it? Did she pull a knife and slit Shuji’s throat?
What about the other people at the party lying cold on the floor? Did she kill them as well?
Did Yuriko imitate Kotomi Ida’s final moments and cut down a swathe of people, all in an effort to spare her own life?
And then… Who turned the knife on Yuriko? Someone acting in self-defense? Did she kill them, too?
There are too many questions and not nearly enough answers to satisfy my hungry mind.
In an effort to find a silver lining in the whole situation, I think about how Kojiro left the body bag at the party.
Hopefully the police will discover the corpse and link Corpse Girl to the murder scene. Her name and website are written all over the HRP, after all.

Everything might work out… As long as Corpse Girl claims the credit for the deaths, my popularity still has a chance of skyrocketing. My/her/my website will be inundated with new requests—requests from people begging for me or Corpse Girl to kill on their behalf.
Yes… Last night’s slaughter may actually be the best thing that could have happened. I’ll happily steal the credit to propel Corpse Girl’s name into the stars.
I roll over and bite my pillow until it’s soaked through with saliva and blood and I scream until my lungs give out.
The house party from hell is all over the news. It’s being live-streamed. It’s all over noise. It’s all anyone is talking about.
I didn’t expect anything less.
A dozen or so people dead. A corpse in a body bag. A cryptic message, ‘WITH LOVE FROM CORPSE GIRL!’
The police are trying desperately to put all the pieces together.

That detective—Shinya’s father—has his face plastered over every news outlet. He says the whole event is linked to the previous string of murders. The ones with corpses decorated to look like the victims.
“Of course it’s linked. You utter dipshit.”
“It’s all Corpse Girl’s doing. It says so on the fucking body bag.”
This wasn’t Corpse Girl’s doing. But the more I lie to myself, the better I feel.
I’m the only one who knows that a copycat was responsible for the deaths.
I’m the only one who has seen the photo with the instructions to kill Shuji.
I’ve still got Yuriko’s phone. That all-important piece of evidence that will surely serve me better than the police.
According to various threads on noise-channel, the police tried to redact the image of the body bag with Corpse Girl’s website written on it.
But once something is on the internet, it’s pretty much impossible to remove it.
The fact that the police wanted it deleted only served to increase the speed at which the image spread.
A thousand posts around the web are all asking the same thing. ‘Who is Corpse Girl?’
Apparently, a lot of people are too scared to visit the website. They fear it might incriminate them—like the police are ready to knock down the door of anyone who visits the site.
Yeah, right.
But that reluctance, that hesitance, hasn’t conquered the hearts of the truly curious.
Corpse Girl’s website has received over a thousand visitors today.
The overwhelming majority of IP addresses accessing the site are based in Tokyo. Even though the murders are known all over Japan, the news outlets in Tokyo are really having a field day with it.
I expected most of the web traffic to be local. But it’s still nice to see some visitors from elsewhere. Osaka. Kyoto. Sapporo. Fukuoka. Hell, there were even two hits from the USA.
Corpse Girl is finally becoming well known.
However… Despite the influx of web traffic, not a single request has been made.
I pout in annoyance as I stare at my laptop screen.
The request inbox shows no unread messages. It’s almost too difficult to believe.

I wonder if the changes I made to the site’s front page have deterred people from using it? I’m asking for a lot more information now—a victim’s name and address are now necessary to submit a request.
I’m about to shut down my laptop in annoyance when a little detail grabs my attention.
The last message in the request inbox…
It’s stamped with a time and date. Today, 5:45pm. About fifteen minutes ago.
Huh…? This request can’t have come through this evening. It’s been marked as ‘read,’ which means I’ve already opened it…
Curious, I click on the message.
The photo that downloads is of somebody I have never seen before. An unremarkable man, but someone that I would instantly recognize if I had previously opened this request.
I return to the inbox and examine the times and dates of each message in closer detail.
Every message is marked as ‘read,’ so I had assumed all of these were requests from previous days. But it would seem that I was wrong.
The messages are all from today. There’s an entire pageful of requests that have been made just since this morning. Twenty-five in total.
Holy shit…
Why are they all marked as ‘read?’ I haven’t seen any of these!
I madly open all of them. The photos of victims quickly download in succession and I skim through them.
Not a single familiar face.
What’s going on…?
As I’m making my way through each message, a brand new request pops up at the top of the screen.
I’m about to click on it when it suddenly turns gray. The tiny little closed envelope icon next to the message transforms into an open envelope right before my eyes.
I’m struck with a single terrifying thought.
Somebody is reading these requests before me…!
Somebody, somehow, has gained access to Corpse Girl’s request inbox. And they are reading every single new request before I do.
Somebody else has access to these requests…!
I can’t believe it. I’m so shocked that I don’t know what to do.
I stare blankly at the screen, my mouth hanging open in disbelief.
Has somebody hacked into my site?
In a desperate bid to regain my composure and a measure of control, I hunch over the laptop and begin tapping at the keyboard.
I access the site’s security settings in order to check the most recent visitors.
All of the traffic is only accessing the front page of the website—as it should be. But one other user has accessed the site’s admin panel directly…!
The security settings show that two people are currently logged in to the admin panel—myself and some stranger!
I look up the IP address of the visitor and find that it’s based in Tokyo.
Perhaps someone who saw the news reports about Corpse Girl decided to try hacking into my website…
I cannot abide a blasphemous transgression like this. How dare they set foot upon my holy soil?!
I’m burning with rage as I click into the site’s advanced security settings.
“I’ll change my password. I’ll ban the hacker’s IP address. I’ll…”
“I’ll kill them!”
“I’ll kill them for defiling Corpse Girl’s website!”
Text_Month="June 18";Text_Day="THURSDAY";Text_Time="Afternoon"
“You heard me.”
“Yeah. So?”
“Can’t you track them down? Don’t you have, like… connections?”
“Already hooked you up with cadavers. Don’t know what else you want.”
“I want you to find this hacker and let me strangle them to death!”
“I’m no computer genius.”
“Take it to the police.”
“You’ve gotta be kidding me.”
“Grr. So what am I supposed to do?”
“Find someone else.”
“Besides. You still owe me.”
“Excuse me? What exactly do I owe you?”
“My share of the corpses.”
“Remember our deal?”
“It’s ‘take take take’ with you.”
“We’re supposed to share.”
“Come on… What do you need me for? You’re capable of getting the cadavers yourself now that you know how.”
“Just ask Tomoe to drive for you.”
“Can I store them at the factory?”
“Store them…? For how long?”
“Don’t know. Weeks?”
“They’ll rot.”
“That’s why I won’t take them home.”
“Ugh. It’ll stink up the whole place.”
“We had a deal…”
“Rrgh! Fine. Store them at the factory. I don’t care.”
“What do you want them for, anyway?”
“Tut, tut, tut. Not allowed to ask.”
“Good luck with your hacker. Got to go.”
“Right… Thanks for nothing.”
“All good in the hood?”
“Sure. Whatever.”
I’m not in the mood for Tomoe right now. I just want to get back to work, get the day over with and go home.
“C’mon. Cheer the fuck up. There’s gotta be someone who can find that hacker.”
“Well, I don’t know anyone.”
“Yeah, me neither…”
“How many requests did yeh say there were?”
“Seventy when I looked this morning.”
“Seventy… Geeeeeeeeez.”
“How’re we gonna deliver that many, uh, ‘yeh-know-whats…?’”
“Keep your voice down!”
“I said ‘yeh-know-whats!’ I didn’t say nothin’ incriminatin’!”
“I don’t know, okay? Is that what you want to hear?”
“Pssht. No need to snap at me.”
“Just shut up for a minute, will you? I can’t think when you’re around.”
“Wow. Sorry.”
“Fuckin’ skank…”
Tomoe’s words hang in the air long after she’s gone. It doesn’t take a genius to figure out that her usage of the word ‘skank’ wasn’t affectionate like usual.
I curse under my breath and return to my desk.
I feel like I’m drowning under stress at the moment.
Everything is piling up on me, forcing me down, pushing my head underwater, and taking away my will to even fight back.
Seventy-odd requests to work through. A hacker with access to my website—even if I’ve managed to block them temporarily, I’m sure they’ll return.
And then there’s the copycat responsible for my sister’s death…
It’s all becoming too much. I don’t feel like I’m in control anymore.
I don’t feel like stoic, unflinching Noriko…
I don’t even feel like Corpse Girl. Poor, defiled Corpse Girl, with hackers prodding her and copycats mocking her…
If I don’t feel like Noriko, and I don’t feel like Corpse Girl…
Then just who the fuck am I?
Text_Month="June 19";Text_Day="FRIDAY";Text_Time="Night"
“Thank you for meeting me after work. I hope you don’t mind eating at this restaurant.”
“Of course. It’s no trouble.”
“It’s nice to see you… I feel like we only ever talk on the phone these days.”
“Um… Is something troubling you?”
I’m not really sure why I asked Aoi to meet me. Part of me wants someone to talk to. I want to vent and unleash my frustrations.
But another deeper, darker part of me just wants to throw everything away and hold her in my arms and let her tell me that everything will be okay.
“Noriko…? You’ve got a weird look on your face.”
“You can talk to me.”
“I… I’m kind of swamped at the moment.”
“Do you ever get that feeling that you’re drowning underneath the weight of everything? That… That no matter what you do, you’ll never escape your situation?”
“What am I saying… Of course you get it. You’ve been through so much shit.”
“Noriko… We’ve both been through a lot. School wasn’t easy for either of us.”
“I know you better than anyone… I know everything about you.”
“That’s true…”
It comforts me when I remember just how close Aoi and I used to be. But… Times have changed. I’ve changed.
I might as well be a completely different person these days.
There are things about me that Aoi doesn’t know. Things that make up who I am—who Corpse Girl is.
“I guess I’m just overwhelmed. Maybe I need a vacation.”
“A vacation, huh…? That does sound nice.”
“Okay! Dream vacation destination… Go!”
“Come on! We used to play this all the time. Don’t think about it. Just tell me about your ideal getaway!”
“Uh… Somewhere… Sunny?”
“Mwe he…”
“Don’t laugh at me…!”
“I just can’t imagine you in the sun… Eh heh heh…!”
“Hmph! Seriously…”
“You said ‘dream vacation,’ so… Yeah, in my dreams, I’d like to go somewhere sunny.”
“Maybe Hawaii. Or Australia.”
“Could you imagine me with a tan…? Ah ha ha!”
“Ha ha!”
“You should go. Go to Hawaii, or Australia, or wherever. Do something good for yourself.”
“Come on. You know it’s not that simple.”
“But why not…?”
“Really? How can you of all people ask me that…?”
“What’s that supposed to mean?”
“You can’t even leave your apartment without checking that the light is off. Or that the faucet isn’t running. You need to check, like, ten or twenty times.”
“Hmph… I’m aware...”
“At least I can go out.”
“Hey. I’m out right now, aren’t I?”
“Are you?”
“Excuse me?”
“Does a safe little place like this even count?”
“How is this any different than your tiny apartment?”
“It’s completely different! I’m surrounded by people, and…”
“It’s the same! You don’t go anywhere new!”
“You’re too terrified to step outside of your comfort zone!”
“Oh, come on! You can’t talk!”
“You couldn’t even start working at the office with me because you were too anxious to leave your apartment!”
“That’s not fair! If… If I’m not certain about everything, then it’s too hard to…”
“Why are we fighting…?”
“We both know what we’re battling with, so… Why?”
“I don’t know… I’m sorry.”
“I’m sorry, too…”
We sit in uncomfortable silence for a while.
Every now and then, Aoi shuffles in her seat and checks her phone.
I said some nasty things to her. Sometimes I talk before I can even think twice about what I’m saying…
“Aoi… Um…”
“Tell me about your dream vacation…”
“I’d actually like to go somewhere colder… I like the cold. I like to wrap up in blankets and sip hot cocoa…”
“Maybe a winter getaway to Switzerland, or Norway…”
“That doesn’t sound half bad… There’s something nice about snuggling up in the cold…”
“Right? I’m glad you agree.”
“You think we’ll ever get away?”
“I’m certain we will.”
“Maybe we could go somewhere together…”
“By the way… I wanted to tell you that I’ll be leaving the maid cafe soon.”
“Really? That’s great!”
“What does your manager think…?”
She pauses before answering. I’m not sure if she’s thinking, or trying to build suspense, or...
“I think he’s had a change of heart.”
“He said I can do what I want.”
“That’s fantastic, Aoi.”
“It’s a relief, that’s for sure.”
“My last shift is tomorrow. After that…”
“After that, I’ll finally be able to escape that one guy…”
Aoi hangs her head. She doesn’t have to say anything more. I know that she’s talking about her stalker—that disgusting guy that makes advances on her at work.
I’m sad that it had to come to Aoi quitting her job in order to escape him, but… A solution is a solution.
“What will you do for work…?”
“I’m sure something will come up.”
“I have a bit of money tucked away, so I’m not too worried.”
“And my boyfriend has a good job, so he can probably help out.”
“Your boyfriend…?”
I’m slightly shocked that Aoi dropped that nugget of information so casually.
Since when has she been seeing somebody? She’s never spoken of a boyfriend before…
A sharp knife carved from jealousy pricks my heart and I have to look away from her in order to hide the tears welling in my eyes.
“We’ve been together for a little while. His name is Junpei! He’s great.”
“Actually, he’s going to pick me up in a little bit.”
Junpei. Junpei. Junpei.
I hate him already. I hate the sound of his name, and I hate the stupid-looking face that my imagination cooks up.
Has he kissed Aoi? Has he touched her?
Has he slept with my Aoi?
I’ll kill him.
I’ll fucking murder him in his sleep.
“I’m so happy for you.”
“Thank you!”
Aoi’s phone vibrates against the table. She glances at the screen and lets out a tiny squeal.
“Oh! He’s here now! I’ll introduce you.”
“Thanks. I’ll ki…”
I cut myself off and ignore Aoi’s quizzical stare.
Aoi stands up and looks toward the door.
She claps her hands in excitement and waves at a broad, bumbling man staggering toward our table.
“Hey babe.”
Junpei. Junpei Junpei Junpei.
Look at this guy. Look at his lecherous eyes, his drooling mouth, his dishevelled clothes…
Aoi is dating this fucker? She could have had anyone she wanted!
She could have had me! She could have had my gorgeous body. I would give myself to her anytime she wants!
She picked Junpei over me…?
“This your friend?”
“Yes! Junpei, this is Noriko.”
“Aoi talks about you a lot.”
“She does...?”
“We’re going to go catch a movie. Would you like to join us, Noriko?”
“Nah, babe. ‘Member, you said we were gonna…”
“It’s fine. I’ve got stuff to do.”
“Oh, okay. Maybe next time!”
“Well, see you!”
Aoi grabs Junpei’s arm and the two lumber away.
I give up.
I clearly can’t compete with what Junpei has to offer her.
I’m over her anyway. I had my chance in senior high school and I blew it.
I’ve moved on. That was my conviction, right? I want her so badly.
But I’ll just keep moving forward. I’ll find someone else. Someone else to fill the void until I can have her.
I’m over her.
I’m over all of this.
Junpei isn’t even worth killing. I don’t have the time to waste on him, anyway.
I have something like seventy requests to work on.
I don’t have time to be relaxing here.
I need to go home and work and fulfill Corpse Girl’s ambitions. If I do that, maybe I can get over Aoi.

And if Corpse Girl becomes famous enough, maybe Aoi will respect me and love me and we can be together and we can go to Hawaii or Australia or Switzerland or Norway and drink hot cocoa in the sun and snuggle up together to stay cold and we can get over our fears and anxieties together and we will always be happy even if Junpei dies and Aoi wouldn’t even care about it and she could just kiss me on the beach and we’d be so happy together.

Everything would be so much better if Corpse Girl could get her shit together and just pull herself up from my mind and not drown in the endless thoughts of ‘what if’ and ‘who’ and ‘why’ that circulate like draining water within my brain.
Everything would be so much better if Aoi just loved me like I love her.
But, for now, I’m over her.
I have work to do.
Each corpse blurs into the next. They all look the same to me now.
Each cause of death is just an insignificant fact. Just a bullet point, a tiny detail to be incorporated into a photo.
I’ve lost track of how many photos I’ve created tonight. Twenty? Thirty?
But the requests keep coming in. I thought there were seventy, but there are so many more now.
Two hundred? Three hundred? I can’t waste my time counting them.
This one is going to die from a baseball bat to the face. This one is going to drown.
This cute guy is going to sever his own head. And this pretty girl will electrocute herself.
They’re all going to leave beautiful corpses. Beautiful corpses in beautiful photos.

We’ll have fun collecting corpses that look like these victims. Me, and Tomoe, and Kojiro. We’ll apply makeup to each corpse, and we’ll dress them up, and we’ll zip them up in cute little body bags and put a nice little ribbon on top and deliver them to our victims.
And each one will die, in turn, and leave behind a beautiful corpse.
Beautiful corpses all over Tokyo. Beautiful, beautiful, beautiful.
Beautiful just like me. So slim, and skeletal, and perfect. So real.
Each corpse will look just a little bit like me. Gorgeous. Kojiro called me gorgeous once.
Aoi has never called me gorgeous.
I don’t have enough burner phones to send out all these photos.
I’ll have to use each phone multiple times. Maybe I can send ten photos from a phone before I dump it.
That’s a good idea. It will reduce the amount of work.
We also won’t have enough room in the van to collect so many corpses from the morgue. We’ll have to make a few trips. Back and forth, from the morgue to the factory to the morgue.
I wonder how many bodies we can fit inside at once. Five? Ten? Fifteen, if we stack them all on top of each other?

I wonder if I could squeeze in between them instead of sitting in the passenger seat? I’m pretty small. I’m pretty skinny. I could probably zip myself up in a body bag and hide amongst the cadavers and pop out and scare Kojiro when he opens up the van to unload them.
Boo! Ha ha. Got you, Kojiro. Bet you didn’t know I was in here with the corpses. Bet I look just like them, don’t I?
Can you unzip a body bag from the inside? I’ll have to try it out.
I can imagine Kojiro’s shocked expression when I pop out, like a naked singer bursting out of a birthday cake. Maybe I could strip down before I get into the body bag. I bet he’d like that.

I bet he’d like to see me slide out of the body bag, completely bare, with my pale skin and my bony arms and my scrawny legs. His eyes would pop out of his skull when he looks at my prominent rib cage and my hips and my tiny, flat breasts.

He’d probably think about it every night before he goes to sleep and fantasize about me and my perfect body and he’d dream about cuddling up with me in the body bag and hiding between the cadavers in the van.
“Ha ha! Got you!”
“Fuck. Fuck!”
“What the fuck, Noriko?”
I pull the top of the body bag down around me and let my chest breathe in the morning sunlight.
“Boo! Boo!”
My naked skin tingles from the fresh air. I don’t think I’ve ever exposed this much skin to the sun.
I giggle and watch Kojiro step back.
“Boo! Got you! Got you!”
“You didn’t know I was in here! Ha ha!”
I wrestle my arms free and make an L shape with my hand. I press it against my forehead.
“Kojiro’s a loser! Loser! Kojiro didn’t know I was in here! Nah nah na na nah!”
“Was wondering why you wouldn’t answer your phone.”
“You’re naked?”
“Boo! Ha ha!”
“Climb in here with me!”
“You okay…?”
“Climb in! Climb in!”
I unzip the body bag further to make room for Kojiro, but he doesn’t advance. He simply stands outside the van, staring at me in disbelief.
“One sec.”
He pulls his phone out of his pocket and presses it to his ear.
“Yeah. Found her.”
“Back of the van.”
“Yeah. In an HRP.”
Kojiro hangs up the phone and puts his hands on his hips.
“Your clothes in here too?”
“Don’t know! But I’m very cold! Come warm me up!”
“You’re lucky we didn’t leave the factory yet.”
“These deliveries can wait. Go inside. Get dressed.”
“Can’t leave the body bag! I’m naked! Ha ha ha!”
Kojiro returns his phone to his face.
“Can you bring her some clothes?”
Kojiro approaches the van. He ducks his head under the roof and stares into my eyes.
“Tomoe is coming outside. She has clothes.”
“Not gonna wear them! I’m a corpse now! I’m Corpse Girl!”
“What the actual fuck…?”
“Noriko! Put these on!”
Tomoe appears from nowhere and thrusts her hand out. In her fist is a shirt and a pair of tracksuit pants, but they don’t belong to me.
“This is all I have with me. Take them!”
I reach out to grab the clothes, but then I push Tomoe’s hand aside at the last second and send the garments flying out of the van.
“Yeh little bitch…!”
“Look at me! I’m a corpse! I’m Corpse Girl!”
“Get inside the body bag with me, Tomoe! I wanna snuggle!”
“Ain’t no way in hell that’s gonna happen.”
“Yeh’ve finally cracked.”
“I think this is serious.”
“No way. Y’think?!”
“She’s lost her mind!”
“We gotta take her home.”
“Noriko. Get out of the van. Sit in the passenger seat.”
“Noriko, please. We’re worried ‘bout yeh. We’re gonna take yeh home.”
“I don’t have a home! I’m a corpse, remember?”
“Take me to the moooooorgue!”
I perform my best corpse impression by sticking my tongue out of my mouth and rolling my eyes back. When nobody laughs, I decide to laugh for them.
“Ah ha ha!”
Kojiro climbs into the van and grabs my wrists.
“Lemme go!”
He forces my arms into the body bag, so they’re pinned by my sides. I can’t fight him off. He’s far stronger than I’ll ever be.
He pulls up the zipper on the body bag until it completely envelops me. Then he pushes me backward so that I fall against the stack of cadavers.

Text_Month="July 30";Text_Day="THURSDAY";Text_Time="Morning"
I try to reflect on life every morning. Keeps me grounded. Keeps my mind busy.
A busy mind is a happy mind.
I like to assess myself. Like I’m judging my own life.
Kojiro. Thirty-four.
Not much more to me than my name.
Done a lot of things. Lot of things I regret.
Lot of things I don’t.
I’m happy, overall. In a better place than I was a year ago.
Stable job. Small group of friends. Couple of hobbies.
Enough to live a satisfying life.
I’ve got ambitions. Desires. Passions.
And fears. Who doesn’t?
I’m clever. At least in my own opinion.
I speak a little French. A lot of Japanese. English not so much.
Dad always told me girls like multilingual guys. Haven’t proven that theory yet.
Been a while since I was in a relationship. And she never cared for my second language.
There’s someone new I’m interested in. She’s strange. Dark. Deep.
Like me.
She doesn’t get me, though. But I get her. I understand everything about her.
Maybe she’ll come around. Maybe not.
That’s probably enough self-reflection for today. I get caught up sometimes. Easy to slip too far inside my mind.
Got things to do today. Deliveries to make. The boss is cracking the whip.
I’ve already eaten breakfast. That’s one thing off my to-do list.
Might need a coffee, though. Should have time to stop by the cafe.
I grab my keys. Phone. Wallet. And a book for the train ride.
Habit of mine to say goodbye to empty rooms. Used to be funny in my school days.
Not so funny anymore. But it’s stuck with me. I find it hard to break habits.
I leave the apartment behind. It occurs to me that it might be the last time.
Probably not. But a possibility.
My mind always thinks of such things. Always prepared for the worst.
Benefit of living near the train station is not having to walk far. But the noise pierces my apartment. I’ve learned to sleep through it.
The platform is quiet today. Must have beaten the rush.
Going straight to the factory today. That blonde girl will drive from there. Tomo? Toma?
Tomoe. Always on the tip of my tongue.
I like the factory. Spent a lot of time there with Dad.
He worked hard. But he always had time for me.
But the factory is different now. Colder. Reminds me too much of the morgue.
Not surprising, though. Not since Noriko made it her home.
She calls it the Corpse Factory.
Not a fan of the name. I like morbid things, but…
The factory meant a lot to me. Now it means nothing.
It’s just a place I go.
I still see Dad there sometimes. I picture him working away.
I know he’s not really there. Just my mind remembering better times.
I miss him a lot.
Hope he’s proud of me.
“Can yeh help me load up?”
The blonde girl is standing by a flatbed trolley. It’s piled high with four cadavers. Each one is sealed in an HRP.
I take the trolley and steer it toward our van. The back door is already open.
A quick peek inside reveals Noriko is not hiding within.
I hoist the first cadaver off the trolley and load it in the van. The second one follows. Then the third.
I wipe a trickle of sweat from my brow. Hot today. Should take off my coat. Maybe later.
One more cadaver on the trolley. Into the van it goes.
“Yer pretty quick at this.”
“I gotta ask… Why’re yeh still helpin’ her?”
“Loyalty? Ha ha.”
“Yeah right…”
“She means a lot to me.”
“Even if I don’t mean much to her.”
“I don’t think anyone means much to her anymore.”
“Might be right.”
I look straight at the girl. Not the type I’d normally associate with.
Girls like her usually think I’m a freak. Or not normal. Either or.
But we’ve gotten to know each other. A little. Wouldn’t call her a friend yet.
“Why do you still hang around?”
“All this shit freaked me out from the start. But…”
“It’s weird. Feels like we’re achievin’ somethin’, y’know?”
“Even if it ain’t right…”
“Just feels like I got a purpose now.”
“I can’t count how many people have died ‘cos of us.”
“The last month has been wild.”
“But I don’t even lose sleep over it anymore.”
“Never did.”
“I’m prolly gonna go to hell.”
“Y’know. For all the bad shit I’ve been doin’.”
“Even if I’m not actually killin’ people… I’m still enablin’ it.”
“Don’t cha ever think we’re gonna go to hell?”
“Don’t believe in the place.”
“I never used to. But…”
“Just been thinkin’ lately, that’s all.”
“But… Between this, and workin’ at the office part-time…”
“I can send some decent cash to my kid brother and sister, y’know?”
“Now that Noriko’s payin’ us, anyway.”
“You’re getting paid?”
“Ah, shit… Yer not…?”
“Joking. I’m getting paid.”
“Phew… That woulda been awkward.”
The girl yawns and shuffles on the spot. She looks back to the factory. The roller door at the loading dock is wide open.
“Bring the trolley?”
She walks away. I grab the trolley and wheel it back to the loading dock.
I abandon the trolley and step inside the factory.
“You here?”
The outline of a sleeping body in the corner begins to stir.
I make my way to the futon lying on the cold concrete floor.
It’s a worn-out thing. Frayed fabric, torn edges.
Lying on top of it, covered by a thin blanket, is the girl of my dreams.
“Huh…? What time is it?”
“Time to get up.”
“Come on…”
“Got work to do.”
“How many deliveries today…?”
“Ask the other girl. I’m just the muscle.”
I reach my hand out to her. Same way I do every morning.
She never takes it.
Instead, she slowly climbs to her feet without assistance.
She’s still wearing yesterday’s clothes. Yesterday’s makeup. Yesterday’s sweat.
She’s gorgeous.
“When are you going back home?”
“This is my home now.”
“You need a shower.”
“I’ll pretend I didn’t hear that.”
“My place smells terrible. Like rotting flesh.”
“I can’t get the odor out. It’s been getting worse since I first moved in there.”
“This place smells too.”
“Look at what’s around you.”
I gesture toward the racks of cadavers that fill the factory.
We acquired some warehouse racking some time ago. It didn’t take long for us to fill most of the shelves with cadavers.
The industrial air conditioner we installed staves off the decay for a little while. But not long enough.
We try not to let each cadaver remain here for more than a few days.
But sometimes we forget.
And it’s so cold here. All the time.
It’s not like Dad’s factory at all.
The stench could make anyone’s eyes water. We just seem to be getting used to it.
“I like it here. The smell here is different…”
“It’s… Nice.”
“You probably have requests to work on.”
“I’ll leave you be.”
Noriko doesn’t say anything. A thoughtful expression covers her face.
I make my way back toward the trolley.
We’ve been overwhelmed with work lately.
Seems like Corpse Girl’s website has become the next big trend in Japan.
Dozens of requests pour in every day. A lot of people are wanted dead.
I don’t care about the reasons why. I just do the work.
It’s all for Noriko. Couldn’t care less about ‘Corpse Girl’s ambitions,’ or whatever she normally says.
I want to prove to her that I’m useful. Good. Worthy.
This is the only way I can think of to earn her love.
I told her I was doing it for corpses. Wanted to get my hands on some for myself.
But that was a lie. All of it.
Why would I need her to acquire corpses? I work at a morgue.
I’ve been stealing them for years.
Just needed her to believe she could motivate me. Bargain with me. Control me.
When she achieves her goal, whatever it may be… I’ll talk to her. A heart-to-heart.
Maybe I’ll even propose.
Can’t let a girl like her slip away. She’s too precious. Too beautiful. Too brooding, and macabre, and…
I need her. It’s as simple as that.
Since the first time I laid eyes on her, over a year ago…
That day she moved into her apartment.
I’ve kept close by ever since.
I must have her.
I will have her.
I’ll do anything for Noriko.
Physical labor always makes me hungry. A normal human trait, I would assume.
I take a seat at the restaurant and place an order once the waitress arrives.
Waiting for a meal is boring. I decide to read.
Today’s book is ‘Fausse Photographie.’ I borrowed it from Noriko. She doesn’t know.
When I flip open the cover I’m reminded of why I started coming here.
I once saw Noriko at this very same restaurant. She was eating omurice and reading ‘Strange Flower.’
She didn’t eat much. Three mouthfuls, if I recall correctly.
But she read her book until the restaurant closed.
I learned then that she’s a girl that would rather feed her mind than her body.
I’m personally the opposite. I love to eat.
But I find Noriko’s traits endearing. It’s hard not to fall for someone in love with educating herself.
It also touched my heart that she chose to read the book I lent her.
Come to think of it… I never did get that back from her.
It’s probably overdue at the library now. Maybe I shouldn’t show my face there again.
Add it to the list of places I can’t visit anymore.
My meal arrives.
I dig in. It’s tasty.
I assume this is Noriko’s favorite. Funnily enough, it was Dad’s favorite too.
I devour the dish in a few minutes. I like to lick the plate clean. Always earns a funny look from the staff.
The heat from the meal has fogged up my glasses. I take them off and wipe them clean on my shirt.

“Kojimbo, right?”

Around the time Noriko targeted her sister, somebody hacked Corpse Girl’s website.
Ever since then, a new string of deaths have raged across Tokyo like wildfire. Deaths not caused by Corpse Girl.

People that were sentenced to death via Corpse Girl’s website were found dead before we could reach them.

He’s here to taunt me. Pressure me.
He knows who I am.
But what’s his endgame?
“Can I try the site?”
“Sure, man!”
“Type the web address into your phone.”
I retrieve my phone from my pocket and enter the site’s address.

I leave the restaurant.
Junpei Matsumoto essentially confessed that he’s involved with The Human Removal Service.

Don’t know if he figured out what I figured out. Don’t care.
I need to tell Noriko.
