It would seem I’ve selected an autobiography about a ‘famed’ painter I’ve never heard of.
It will do for now. I’ll read anything.
I skim through the preface. Then the first chapter.
My fingers pick up speed as I thumb through the pages, never absorbing more than the first line of any particular page.
Boring. Drivel. I can’t read this.
I toss the book aside and rest a closed fist underneath my chin.
I’m not normally this restless. Usually, I’m focused and driven.
But it’s my birthday. And Shizuko isn’t here to get me a gift.
Perhaps I regret throwing away the French press. It was the most thoughtful birthday gift I’ve ever received.
Perhaps I just regret losing Shizuko. I don’t know.
If this were any other day, I wouldn’t waste my time dwelling on the past. I thought I was above giving this day more significance than any other.
Thirty-five. Fuck. Where do the years go?
Time really does slip through your fingers.
Hell, it’s even been more than a year since I met Noriko. Technically. I doubt she remembers our first meeting.
I peer around the library and find a smile forming on my face.
She probably thinks we met here just a few months ago. I asked her some trivial question. Something about Lovecraft, or Cthulhu. Then I introduced myself.
But the first time we bumped into each other was at my apartment. Well, her apartment.
It was a fully furnished apartment. Didn’t have to take much with me when I left.
I bet it looks much the same today as it did back then.
I returned to collect a few last things. A couple of blankets in the closet. A broom and a dustpan. A few knuckle bones. The usual stuff.
And I wanted to say goodbye, one final time.
To my surprise, she was there. She was chatting to the landlord casually, inquiring about the terms of the lease.
I must have frozen in my tracks when I saw her. I know that I spent a good few minutes simply staring at her.
She was beautiful. Gorgeous. Breathtaking.
And she looked like Shizuko. She looked so much like Shizuko…
She shook hands with the landlord. She said her name aloud. Noriko Kurosawa.
Her name stuck in my mind. It replayed over and over in my head.
The landlord accepted her offer for the apartment. Noriko would be moving in, making the place her home. My place.
I must have bumped my shoulder into her by accident when I tried to squeeze past.
She apologized. I apologized.
“Soz. Was just leaving.”
“Oh no, please. It was my fault. I’m very sorry.”
“Um… Did you live here?”
“I see. Thank you for taking care of the place. I’ll be moving in soon.”
“I see.”
“Did you like it here?”
“Yes. Very much so. It… It was home.”
“I’m glad. I hope that I feel just as comfortable here.”
I nodded, but didn’t pull my eyes from her face.
She walked away after gracing me with a polite bow.
The Noriko from back then was healthier than the girl I know now.
She’s become little more than a skeleton. Skin and bones. But her keen mind hasn’t dulled.
And she’s still gorgeous. Still takes my breath away. Just like Shizuko once did.
But she refuses to leave the factory.
She refuses to return to her apartment.
Occasionally Tomoe will go and fetch the things she needs. Clothes. Tiny portions of food. Coffee, mostly.
At some point, I got delegated to selecting the most suitable cadavers from the morgue. All so Noriko doesn’t have to visit the morgue herself.
She gives me a bunch of photos, and it’s on me to pick and choose cadavers that best match them.
Not my favorite work. It’s tedious. And I don’t have the eye for detail that she does.
But I do what I can.
My phone begins vibrating violently in my back pocket. I didn’t realize I was sitting on it.
“Where the hell are you?”
“Don’t you have deliveries to make today?”
“I’m just taking the morning off.”
“Tsk. You didn’t ask me about that…”
“I told Tomoe.”
“Well, she didn’t mention anything about it to me…”
“Soz. I’ll see you in a few hours, anyway.”
“I just wanted to chill this morning.”
“My birthday.”
“It’s your birthday…?”
“I didn’t know…”
“Happy birthday.”
“Okay… I’ll see you this afternoon.”
She sounded mad at me.
In my defense, I haven’t taken a day off from Corpse Girl’s work for weeks. Didn’t think taking this morning off would be too much to ask.
Apparently it rubbed her the wrong way.
But juggling this work as well as my morgue duties is tiring. Don’t get much time for myself.
Don’t get much time to think.
Probably why Shizuko’s face doesn’t pop into my mind as much as it used to. My theory, anyway.
I drain the remnants of my coffee cup.
After returning the unread book to the shelf, I leave the library.
“I’m home.”
I close the front door behind me. My place is always dark. The tiniest sliver of sunlight filters in from a gap between the closed curtains.
I like it this way. I spend countless nights underneath the unholy lights of the morgue. That fluorescent glow messes with my eyes.
So I keep my apartment dark. It’s comforting.
The place is small. Smaller than my last apartment, at any rate. Noriko’s apartment.
A tiny living space. One bedroom. A kitchenette.
The bathroom is pitiful. A half-sized tub, with a showerhead above it. A toilet. No sink—I need to use the kitchen sink after finishing my business.
But it’s home. Moving here after deciding to leave my old place was the change I needed after Shizuko died.
I threw away so much of my life from back then. I’m almost a completely different person now.
I’ve kept my habits. Mannerisms. The parts of me people find weird or off-putting. Can’t help it. That’s just how I am.
All those quirky attributes that Shizuko couldn’t stand.
They’re still with me.
She’s gone, and I’m still here.
“Come on.”
I shake my head at the sound of my own voice.
What a birthday. What a pointless day.
Dwelling on the past doesn’t suit me. I moved on from Shizuko a long time ago.
I’m only stuck on her today because of my birthday. Because this day reminds me of that damn French press she bought for me.
But it’s gone now. And she’s gone.
All that remains is me.
That’s the way it always has been. Probably the way it always will be.
“Time for work.”
I don’t feel like staying in and relaxing.
I shuffle toward the tall, narrow cabinet in the far corner of my living space.
I hoist the door open and look at my clean white coat. It’s not stained or dusty like the one I keep on display near the window.
It’s my good coat. The one I reserve for special days. Like my birthday...
The white coat is resting comfortably on a white mannequin inside the white cabinet. I hate the color white. It serves no purpose.
Despite its useless color, the mannequin holding the coat does serve a purpose. It carries my treasured possessions.
Perhaps ‘mannequin’ isn’t the most fitting word for it. But it will do.
As I grab my coat, the sleeve catches on the mannequin’s fingers.
I tug at it gently and manage to release the coat from the mannequin’s bony limb.
Habit of mine to say goodbye to empty rooms. Used to be funny when rooms were truly empty.
Not so funny anymore. Not when that face stares back at me from within the cabinet.
Nothing to do about it.
“Happy birthday.”
“I don’t have a gift for you… I’m sorry.”
“All good.”
Noriko runs her hand along her opposite arm shyly. Not like her to act so awkward and embarrassed.
“I… I just didn’t know. That’s all.”
“I know.”
She seems truly disappointed in herself for not knowing about my birthday.
“I looked at my noise feed, and it even has a notification that today’s the day…”
“I’m sorry. I don’t have a reasonable excuse.”
“It’s fine. Really.”
“What’s on the agenda today?”
I want to break away from this discussion. I hate my birthday. I hate Shizuko for leaving me.
Noriko sweeps a stray strand of hair behind her ear and contemplates the question.
“Twelve deliveries. Tomoe has already prepped the bodies. She’s waiting in the van. I’ve sent the photos to the victims.”
“Only twelve today?”
“We’re not getting many new requests. All of today’s deliveries are just part of our backlog.”
“There aren’t many corpses left here, actually.”
“We’ve managed to work our way through most of them.”
“Have to visit the morgue again soon…”
“I see.”
“Things seem to be slowing down…”
“The copycat is stealing our business. I just know it.”
“Oh! That reminds me… Whatever happened to Aoi’s boyfriend?”
“What do you mean?”
“I can’t believe I forgot about it… You were going to kill him.”
“Oh. Yeah.”
Somehow, I’d forgotten about that, too. Caught up in my own head today.
Junpei Matsumoto.
“Is he dead?”
Noriko’s pout prompts me to explain.
“Hurt him good. But Aoi arrived before I could go further.”
“Did she see you?”
“She doesn’t know me, though.”
“I suppose…”
“Wait. You didn’t hurt Aoi, did you?”
The tone of panic in her gasping voice is impossible to disregard.
“‘Course not.”
“Aoi’s innocent, you know? She can’t get caught up in all this…”
“I know...”
I’d never hurt a friend of Noriko’s.
Unless they hurt me first. Self-defense, or something.
“So what do we do about Junpei? If he’s still alive... He knows that you’re involved with the morgue, and with Corpse Girl…”
“...Don’t know.”
“Actually. He did say something interesting.”
“What did he say?”
“I quote, ‘Every person targeted by The Human Removal Service is removed by the Herald’s hand.’ End quote.”
“The Herald…?”
“Who the fuck is the Herald?”
“Did you mishear? Was it supposed to be Gerald?”
“Herald. Apparently some prophet. A visionary.”
“Junpei says he’s immortal.”
“Immortal…? You’re not serious.”
“Mm. Every killing is carried out by him personally.”
“What the hell…?”
“How is that even possible? How can someone kill so many people without getting caught?”
I shrug. My tongue subconsciously licks the gap where my tooth once was.
“Guess he’s good.”
“Ugh. What a pain in the ass.”
“Anyway. I’ll take care of those deliveries.”
“I’m going to try and dig up something.”
“Dig up?”
“Not literally. Information. Online.”
“Had me excited there for a moment.”
“Don’t worry. You’ll be the first person I tell if I decide to go digging up bodies.”
“Ha. Thanks.”
I throw Noriko a lazy wave and take my leave.
“Yeh finally good to go?”
“Good. I wanna get this over with.”
“Oh. Happy birthday, by the way.”
It’s funny to think that Tomoe knows about my birthday. I assume she read about it on noise, since we’re now ‘friends.’
“Get any prezzies?”
“Not one.”
“Lame. Whaddya like? I’ll buy yeh somethin’.”
“Really? You’d do that for me?”
“Of course! Yeh may be a creep, but birthdays are the best! Everyone deserves a present.”
I think she’s being nice. Not a fan of being called a creep.
“I’d like a French press.”
Would I…?
“What’s that?”
“A coffee press.”
“Oh! I know those. Yeah, sure. I’ll order yeh one. Cool?”
“Cool. Thanks.”
“Sure! Happy birthday, Kojiro.”
Surprisingly, she steps forward to give me a short hug.
It feels nice.
She’s warm. Not like Noriko—or the way I imagine Noriko to be.
Her hair smells wonderful. Like coconut. I’m not sniffing it on purpose. I’m not trying to play up to my reputation as a creep. But it’s impossible not to smell it when we’re this close.
Her fingers tap against my back a few times, and then she releases the hug.
A smile as warm as her touch spreads across her face.
“C’mon. Let’s get goin’.”
Tomoe opens the van’s driver-side door and scoots inside.
As the door shuts behind her, I can’t help but entertain the thought of what she would be like to have as a girlfriend. A partner. A lover.
She’s nicer than I originally thought. Heart’s in the right place.
But she’s not Noriko.
I shake the fleeting thoughts from my mind and urge myself to get on with things.
Delivery time.
Text_Month="August 2";Text_Day="SUNDAY";Text_Time="Night"
Morgue duties have felt mundane lately. Boring. Pointless.
Lots of things I’d rather be doing.
Had to come in early today thanks to an influx of deceased patients from the hospital.
Bodies get passed through the hospital halls and land in my lap. Unceremoniously.
They need tagging. Need to be added to inventory. Need to be stored.
Cadavers are needier than some people.
Don’t know where I’m going to store this lot.
Running out of room in this place. Only a handful of cold chambers still available.
I can thank The Human Removal Service for that.
This isn’t the only morgue in the area, but it’s one of the biggest. A lot of cadavers end up here.
A lot of victims.
Weeks ago, I used to smile every time one of Corpse Girl’s victims entered this hallowed place.
It was kind of poetic.
Noriko cherry-picked corpses from this morgue. Those corpses were delivered to victims.
The victims died, and they ended up here as fresh cadavers.
Ready to repeat the cycle.
It was beautiful. The circle of death.
Now… It’s rare for Corpse Girl’s victims to arrive. More common are the victims of The Human Removal Service. At least… That’s my speculation.
When multiple homicide victims arrive on your doorstep every day, it’s not hard to piece things together.
Lacerations. Dismembered limbs. Rope marks. Bludgeoned skulls.
Myriad mortal wounds inflicted on the flesh.
I always suspected Corpse Girl’s copycat was behind the sheer amount of deaths raging across Tokyo.
Seeing the fruits of the copycat’s labor first-hand has convinced me that we’re not dealing with simple suicides.
And Junpei Matsumoto’s words still ring clearly in my ears. ‘Our Herald… He carries out all the killings personally…’
It all adds up.
Corpse Girl has truly met her match.
While The Human Removal Service continues to claim countless lives, Corpse Girl’s success is rapidly declining.
Much to Noriko’s chagrin, Corpse Girl has become so well-known that the general public no longer fears her.
Like a figure from folklore, or a fictional character… Everybody knows the name Corpse Girl, but only the truly gullible believe she can kill people.
I call it the Bloody Mary Effect.
If someone is predisposed to believe in a horrific entity, they will convince themself that said entity truly exists.

When targeted by Corpse Girl, such a person will succumb to suicide in an attempt to escape a potentially more grisly fate. In reality, they simply play right into the trap that Corpse Girl laid for them.

Those that treat Corpse Girl as no more than an entertaining piece of folklore—like Bloody Mary—are immune to the fear. Someone like this can receive a photo of their own corpse and shrug it off as no more of a threat than a spam email.
It’s ironic that the success Noriko sought for so long is the very thing that has rendered Corpse Girl’s methods ineffective.
I wouldn’t say all of this to Noriko’s face. She’s well aware of the situation.
As for The Human Removal Service…
No one seems to know about it. There’s no mention of it anywhere on the internet—anywhere I can access, at any rate.
Police investigating the string of homicides haven’t mentioned it.
If the site relies on users to request deaths, I am at a loss as to how people are learning about it.
It truly seems to be some sort of shadow organization… Except for the fact that Junpei Matsumoto essentially walked right up to me and revealed himself.
I don’t know his motives for doing so.
And I don’t know how he found out I’m involved with Corpse Girl’s work.
I really should take care of him.
Text_Month="August 3";Text_Day="MONDAY";Text_Time="Morning"
A knock at the door.
I rub my eyes and sit up slowly.
Must have fallen asleep in my chair again.
Still groggy, I get up and look through the front door’s peephole.
A single, lonely package sits on the doormat.
Don’t know where it came from. Haven’t ordered anything online lately.
I swing the door open and pick up the plain brown parcel. Something rattles inside.
Bringing it indoors, I slip my thumb underneath the packing tape and tear it open.
Nestled on a bed of packing foam is a white box adorned with the image of a French press.
“A coffee maker…”
That’s right. This is a gift from Tomoe.
She really bought me a birthday gift. Something that I truly wanted.
My friend, Tomoe…
After putting the package down, I retrieve my phone and open up noise.
THank you for the birthday present.
u got it already??????
Just now. It’s a good brand, too.
sweet!! ~~ ^.^ glad u like it~~
MAybe I’ll brew you a cup one day.
Ha ha.
yus pls~~
extraa sugar “0.0”
You got it.
Tomoe doesn’t send a follow-up message. I take that to mean the conversation has expired.
It feels good that she did such a nice thing for me.
Almost forgotten what it’s like to have someone care.
Pity she has a boyfriend. Never stops going on about him.
Regardless, it doesn’t matter. I shouldn’t misconstrue a kind gesture as affection. She was simply bestowing a birthday gift.
Something most people would do for a friend.
Something Noriko didn’t even attempt.
Don’t know how to break down Noriko’s barriers. Been trying for a long time. She just never seems to warm up.
Maybe chasing her is a lost cause.
But I’m tired of being lonely. I’m so tired.
Noriko. Tomoe. I don’t care… If either of them would accept me, I would give them everything I am.
I just don’t want to be alone anymore.
The start of another long night.
Alone, like always.
The cadavers can hardly be called company.
They don’t speak. Don’t laugh at my jokes. Not like living people laugh at my jokes, anyway.
“Hey. I think I mentioned this a day or two ago, but our reserves have pretty much dried up.”
She means her stash of corpses at the factory. She has a way with words.
“Anyway. Three new requests came through today. I’m really excited.”
“Maybe things will pick up again?”
“I’ll send through photos of the vics. Can you select some corpses that resemble them?”
“Tomoe will come by with the van.”
“Are you okay? You’re pretty quiet. More than usual, anyway.”
“I’m fine.”
“I see…”
“Well, thanks. I’m sending the photos now. Message me when you’re done. I’ll send Tomoe over.”
I end the call and return my phone to my pocket.
It vibrates three times in quick succession as Noriko’s photos automatically download.
Three requests. Not much, but enough to lift her spirits.
I scan the array of cold chambers lining the walls. This place is packed to the gills. Shouldn’t be a problem to find some matches for her.
I take a stroll alongside the left row of chambers. All of the bodies within are due for cremation.
I can take my pick from here. Just like always. Business as usual.
I fish my phone out once more and examine the new photos.
Two women. One man.
Middle-aged. Young adult. Young adult.
Normal, everyday people.
Corpse Girl will wrap her fingers around their throats and try to kill them.
Will they shrug off the attempt on their lives?
Time will tell.
I’ll do my best to help Noriko end their lives.
I wander toward the computer at the end of the room and log in to the inventory system.
Time to find some suitable bodies.
Text_Month="August 4";Text_Day="TUESDAY";Text_Time="Afternoon"
“The corpses you picked out are good. Two of them, anyway.”
“What’s wrong with the third?”
“He looks a bit too old. Older than the victim, at any rate.”
“I see.”
“It’s not a problem. I think it will still be convincing.”
“Are we delivering them today?”
“No. I received even more requests overnight. I need you to go select more cadavers.”
“Sheesh. Again?”
“Aren’t you happy that we’re busy again?”
“Couldn’t care less.”
“I’m only doing this for you.”
It’s the truth. Even if she doesn’t want to hear it.
“I heard that Tomoe got you a birthday gift.”
“Way to change the subject.”
“I’m sorry.”
“I’m supposed to be your friend, and I was just so caught up within my own head that I couldn’t be bothered with your birthday.”
“It’s fine.”
It’s not fine.
“So… If you’ll accept a late gift… Is there anything you would like?”
“A date.”
“With you.”
“Anything else…?”
“You’re being awfully forward today. I thought we agreed to just be friends.”
“What’s gotten into you?”
“Forget it.”
I have to look away from her to prevent her from seeing the snarl on my face.
“I’ll go pick out some cadavers for you.”
“Okay… Bye…”
I step away and mutter to myself.
I’m so stupid.
Why am I acting so desperately around her all of a sudden?
“What kinda hello is that?”
“Soz. In a mood.”
“Always the case with yeh, ain’t it?”
“Seems to be.”
She gets me.
“Listen. How ‘bout that cup of coffee yeh promised me?”
“Y’know… C’mon. Don’t make me say it.”
“Yeh said yeh’d brew me some coffee with that French press thing.”
“And, well… I could really use a cup, y’know?”
“Oh. Yeah. I remember.”
“Soz. Noriko has sent me to the morgue.”
“Why? She kill yeh?”
Takes me a second to get that she’s joking.
“Oh. Aha.”
Tomoe smiles warmly and waves her finger in the air.
“I’m gonna go ahead and guess that it ain’t every day a pretty girl offers to have coffee with yeh.”
“So, are we doin’ this, or what?”
I can’t fathom a reason for Tomoe’s recent shift of attitude toward me.
When we first started working together, she could hardly tolerate being in the same room as me.
And now she wants me to brew coffee for her?
Does she want something from me?
Is she in love with me?
No. She’s not. Definitely not.
No one loves me.
Even so, I don’t want to be alone.
How can I refuse her offer?
“Okay. I can put off the morgue until later.”
“Yeh finally came to yer senses, huh?”
“Well, c’mon then! Let’s go to yer place. I’ll drive.”
My place…
The last time a girl visited my home…
It was back when I lived in Noriko’s apartment. Back when Shizuko…
Clucking my tongue serves to distract me from the painful memories.
“Let’s go.”
“This is yer place, huh?”
“It’s freakin’ dark in here.”
“Yeh a vampire or somethin’?”
“‘Course not. I was just outside in the sun with you.”
“True that.”
Tomoe looks around the small room and stands uncomfortably by the wall.
“Yeh don’t bring girls back here very often, do yeh…”
“Maybe if yeh made the place look more appealin’, then girls just might wanna come back here.”
“You’re here.”
“Sure, but I’m complainin’, ain’t I?”
“Why are you here, anyway? It’s not for coffee. Is it?”
“Yer a sharp one, ain’t cha?”
“I wanted to talk to yeh away from… Y’know.”
“Your boyfriend?”
“No! Geez. Away from Noriko.”
“This whole thing’s been goin’ downhill, wouldn’t yeh agree?”
“All this shit with tryin’ to make people off ‘emselves…”
“Sure, I’m used to it by now, but…”
“Shit’s started to hit the fan.”
“How so?”
“Well, there’s the business with… What was it? The Human Removal Service?”
“Noriko told you about that?”
“Yeah, ‘course. We’re besties, y’know?”
“They been out there killin’ and killin’, and the police wanna shift all the blame onto Corpse Girl.”
“After all, Corpse Girl is the only killer that has gone public.”
“Her name and website are written all over the body bags we deliver…”
“People talk, and everyone knows about her.”
“So, ‘course the police are gonna assume she’s behind all the murders.”
“‘Cept… She’s not. Not really.”
“A handful of ‘em, here and there, but even then, they’re just suicides.”
“Corpse Girl—Noriko—she ain’t out there slashin’ necks and drownin’ people and settin’ houses on fire.”
“She ain’t doin’ any of that shit goin’ down on the news.”
“I know all this.”
“Yeah, yeah.”
“I’m just sayin’...”
“If things keep up at this rate, the cops are gonna find her. Noriko.”
“And she’s gonna get locked up for life.”
“I ain’t gonna lie. She deserves it. The stuff she’s doin’ is messed up.”
“Thing is… Me and yeh? We’re accomp… Accomplish…”
“Yeah. That.”
“We’re in neck-deep. If Noriko gets put on ice, we get taken along with her.”
“Hmm. I see.”
“You’re worried about going to prison.”
“‘Course I am! I’ve got people to take care of.”
“What would Shinya do if I got locked up? What would he think o’ me?”
“Not to mention my little brother and sister…”
Tomoe’s crestfallen countenance makes the room feel darker than it truly is.
Her watery eyes break away from mine and she tries hard to restrain herself from sobbing.
“I can’t…”
“I don’t think I can do this anymore.”
“No matter how much she pays me, I just…”
“I just can’t keep riskin’ it…”
I understand. This is difficult for her.
She’s torn between loyalty to a friend and her own freedom.
“I think your course of action is clear.”
“It is…?”
“Yes. You need to step away from the game.”
“It won’t do us any good if you’re not totally invested.”
“You could make a fatal mistake that has consequences for all of us.”
“If you’re not committed, not focused… It’s best that you part ways with Noriko.”
“Y’know… Yeh really are more understandin’ than yeh look…”
“I thought yeh were a total social outcast, with no feelings or empathy…”
“Let me finish. I… I was wrong.”
“Yer alright, Kojiro.”
“I’ll… I’ll take yer advice.”
“I’ll talk to Noriko, and tell her I ain’t cut out for this anymore.”
“It’s for the best.”
“I guess we won’t hang out anymore.”
“Do we ever hang out? Ha ha…”
“Well… Our deliveries, our time at the factory…”
“Dunno. Kind of grew to like it.”
“Oh, shit…”
“I forgot. There’s somethin’ I still need to do for Noriko.”
“What’s that?”
“She asked me to go to her apartment and pick up some clean clothes for her.”
“I owe her that much, at least.”
“Yeh wanna come with me?”
“Her apartment…?”
Noriko’s apartment. My apartment.
Not anymore. I haven’t lived there for a while… But it will always feel like mine.
I wonder if there are any old memories to find between its walls?
“Okay. I’ll come with you.”
“Do I need to break any windows?”
“No! ‘Course not… Noriko gave me her keys.”
“I see.”
“Yeh sound disappointed!”
I shrug and let her accusation slide.
I didn’t expect a flood of mundane recollections to drown my mind as soon as I started climbing the staircase.
This place has such a hold over me.
My past life… My life with Shizuko.
It’s so foggy but so familiar.
I don’t even feel like the same person I was back then.
But of course I’m the same. I’m still me.
And the stench ingrained in these walls…
“Every time I come in here it smells worse ‘n worse…”
“What is it?”
“...Don’t know.”
Mold? Mildew?
No. It’s more sickening than that. It’s something rotten.
“Yuck. Anyway, her place is up just a few more levels.”
“I know...”
“Oh. Yeh been here before?”
Tomoe abandons her thoughts in the air and continues to climb the stairs.
When we reach the landing below Noriko’s floor, a young girl’s voice rings out.
MomoName="? ? ?"
It doesn’t take long to identify the owner of the voice.
A girl, no older than seven, is knocking repeatedly on the door of an apartment.
She notices our arrival.
“Who… Who are you…?”
“Hello there. My name is Tomoe. What’s yer name?”
“Nice to meet you, Momo. Do you live here?”
“The door is locked… I can’t get inside.”
“I see.”
Somehow, the girl has locked herself outside her own apartment.
“Is your mommy or daddy home?”
“I think daddy is home, but he won’t answer the door.”
“Let me try, okay?”
The young girl hesitantly nods, nervousness evident on her features.
Tomoe slams her fists against the apartment door, unafraid of holding back her strength.
“Yo! Anyone home up in here?”
“Hellooooo! Anyone there?”
After a good thirty seconds of pounding the door, Tomoe puts her hands on her hips.
“Are yeh sure yer dad is home right now?”
“I think so… He was here right before I went outside to play.”
Tomoe grimaces and looks me dead in the eyes.
“Yeh don’t think somethin’ happened, do yeh…?”
“Don’t know.”
I crouch down and rest my weight on one knee so that I come face-to-face with the girl.
“What’s your dad’s name?”
“Umm… It’s Kenji…”
“Kenji, huh…”
“And what was he doing before you went to play?”
Momo twiddles her fingers uncomfortably. Her expression turns thoughtful as she tries to remember.
“He was watching TV.”
“I see. Thank you.”
I stand back up and turn to Tomoe.
She raises an eyebrow as if in disbelief of the polite persona I adopted to talk to the girl.
“If he’s got the TV on, it might be too loud for him to hear us.”
“Anyway, I’m sure he’ll open the door soon.”
“We should go up to Noriko’s.”
“Yer unbelievable!”
“I ain’t leavin’ this girl here!”
“What if somethin’ bad happened to her dad?!”
“Something happened to dad…?”
“No! Oh, honey, I didn’t mean it like that.”
“Kojiro, we need to get in there—”
Tomoe’s sentence is cut off as the apartment door suddenly opens.
A formidable man, broad-shouldered and with a smoldering expression, now inhabits the open doorway.
“Clear the doorway.”
He takes one look at Momo and then turns his neck to bark at somebody behind him.
“The daughter is right here.”
“Bring her with us. Hurry it up!”
The stern man pushes past me and I stumble as I try to get out of his way.
I don’t like being pushed around, but the sight of half a dozen uniformed police officers shuffling out of the apartment behind him encourages me not to retaliate.
Dragged along behind one of the officers is a handcuffed man in disheveled clothes.
“Momo…! Oh, thank god…”
“Sweetie… Daddy has to go to the police station for a little bit.”
“I’m sorry, sweetie… I’m so sorry…”
Before he can squeeze out another word, the police officers yank him away from his daughter.
He is accompanied downstairs and disappears from view within moments.
“Daddy…! Come back, Daddy!”
The final police officer to exit the apartment bends down in front of Momo. He mumbles something to her, then grabs her shoulders in an attempt to steer her toward the staircase.
“Let go of me! Daddy!”
“What the fuck is goin’ on here…?”
Tomoe takes a step toward the officer, her fingers slowly curling into a fist.
I clutch her fist in my own and force her to lower it.
“Don’t get involved.”
“It’s a police matter.”
I think she understands my vague warning, as she stops struggling against me.
The young girl is escorted downstairs, and Tomoe stands defeated next to me.
“What the hell just happened…?”
Tomoe is uncharacteristically quiet as she searches Noriko’s apartment for clean clothing.
Witnessing that man—Kenji—get arrested in front of his own daughter seems to have dampened Tomoe’s spirits.
Although he’s a stranger, I can’t help but feel bad for the guy. Don’t know what he did wrong, but surely his daughter didn’t need to see that going down.
“You okay?”
Tomoe ignores me as she rifles through Noriko’s drawers.
I decide to bite my tongue and simply take a seat on the edge of the bed.
The first man to leave that apartment… The guy with broad shoulders…
He looked familiar. Very familiar.
Seemed to be in charge of the officers.
A detective?
Yes, that’s it.
A police detective. I’ve seen him on TV a few times lately.
He’s the one heading up the investigation of the recent homicides.
The one accusing Corpse Girl of being the culprit behind The Human Removal Service’s string of murders.
The man he apprehended… Kenji…
Is he involved with the case? Is he a suspect?
Is he the Herald?
A neighbor of Noriko’s… Could it truly be?
Could Kenji truly be the leader of The Human Removal Service?
I try to connect all the dots in my mind.
He lives close to Noriko. He might even be on speaking terms with her.
He might have access to Noriko’s computer, her website…
Could he have been the original hacker, stealing Corpse Girl’s requests? The copycat?
It all seems coincidental, but…
It almost makes sense. It’s more likely than not that the copycat is someone who personally knows Noriko. Someone who has an inside view of her life.
But what’s his motive?
Looked like a normal guy. Just a father living with his daughter.
What could have inspired him to embark on a killing spree?
Actually, for that matter…
What inspired Noriko to do the same in the first place…?
Never mind that. It’s irrelevant right now.
Are you the one we’ve been looking for? Are you allied with Junpei Matsumoto?
Are you the prophet, the Herald, the one capable of standing toe-to-toe with Corpse Girl?
“Okay. I’m done.”
I blink a few times and look at Tomoe. She’s standing with a pile of clothes neatly nestled in her arms.
“Can we get goin’?”
Leaving now is for the best.
I want to get home. Want to spend some time with my thoughts.
There’s a lot of new information to sort through…
Complete Act II.
Text_Month="August 5";Text_Day="WEDNESDAY";Text_Time="Morning"
Not a morning person. Never have been.
But running with Noriko has forced me to get up early more times than I can count.
Doesn’t mean I’m getting used to it. Still can’t prevent myself from yawning.
Doesn’t help that last night was a sleepless one.
Couldn’t convince my overactive mind to take a break.
Even distractions didn’t help. Couldn’t concentrate on reading. Couldn’t focus on tidying the apartment.
Nothing worked.
The same questions kept bouncing around the inside of my skull.
When the sun came up, I decided to stop torturing myself and just confront Noriko.
Perhaps she has some answers.
“Wake up.”
I lean over her near-lifeless body and whisper sharply.
Don’t want to scare her awake. Don’t want her to ignore me, either.
“Noriko. Wake up.”
My whisper becomes more of a hiss and the girl before me begins to stir.
She rubs her eyes. A familiar sight thanks to all the times I’ve woken her up lately.
“Again, Kojiro…?”
“What time is it?”
“Listen. Got some questions for you.”
“Give me a break…”
She sighs, sits up, and reaches for her handbag lying next to her futon.
After rummaging through its contents for a few seconds, she curses under her breath.
“No coffee…”
I toss her a silver can of coffee I picked up from a vending machine on the way over.
I know the drill by now. Know Noriko well.
The can slips through Noriko’s slender fingers and comes to rest safely in her lap.
She cracks open the tab and takes a long sip, effectively draining half the contents in one swig.
“This is nice.”
She thoughtfully examines the front of the can, running her fingers along the embossed logo.
“Glad you like it. Now. Questions.”
“Pfft. Fine. Go.”
“Do you know a guy named Kenji? With a daughter. Momo.”
Noriko cocks her head to the side as if this was the last question she expected to hear from me.
“Er… Yeah. I know them.”
“They’re my neighbors. Kind of. They live on the floor below me.”
“That’s right.”
“You on speaking terms?”
“More or less.”
Her eyes dart away from mine and she takes a moment to think.
“Momo’s sweet. A nice girl.”
“Kenji… We used to talk, but then…”
“Well, I think he’s lost respect for me. Let’s leave it at that.”
“I see.”
“This is weird. How do you know those two?”
Suppose it can’t hurt to tell her. Tomoe probably will, if I don’t.
“Went to your apartment yesterday. With Tomoe.”
“You did?”
“Had to collect clothes for you.”
“Going upstairs, we saw Kenji get arrested by the police.”
“Lots of cops. And that detective from TV.”
“Wait. Kenji got arrested?”
“Don’t know.”
“They took him away in cuffs. Took Momo, too.”
“The detective… You’re not talking about the one heading up the murder investigations, are you?”
“That’s him. Big guy.”
“Huh. Fujikawa?”
Interesting. Didn’t know his name before. Detective Fujikawa… Not exactly the type I want to cross.
Noriko’s shoulders slump.
“Poor Kenji…”
“I wonder why he got arres…”
A flicker of realization flashes across her face.
Within a split-second, Noriko’s defeated expression gives way to a hideous, wicked smile. Her eyes narrow and a shrill laugh pierces my ears.
“Aha ha ha ha!!”
“That’s fantastic…!”
Don’t know if she’s lost the plot, or if she’s figured something out.
“All those precautions I took… All that preparation…”
“It finally paid off…!”
“Spill it. What are you talking about?”
“Okay. Ah ha ha…”
“Right. Listen carefully.”
“When this all started… When Corpse Girl first told me to start killing…”
When Corpse Girl first told her…?
I thought she was Corpse Girl. That’s what she’s always referred to herself as…
“I knew that running the website from my apartment was a risk.”
“I knew accessing the Database of the Deceased could be tracked by anyone watching me…”
“I took certain measures to protect myself. To protect Corpse Girl’s work.”
“What did you do…?”
“I pinned everything on Kenji Ogawa…”
“I used his internet service—his WiFi. I used his address for registering my website.”
“I used his name for every service I signed up to…”
“Everything I did created a trail of breadcrumbs that would point to Kenji in the event that the authorities ever came looking for Corpse Girl.”
Noriko planned everything from the start with a great amount of forethought.
More concerning is the fact that she wasn’t afraid to throw her neighbor to the wolves in order to save her own skin…
Still, if I take Noriko at her word, this rules Kenji out as the mastermind behind The Human Removal Service. He couldn’t be the Herald that Junpei Matsumoto spoke of.
He was just a scapegoat. Wrong place, wrong time.
“Clever. I’m impressed.”
“Thank you…”
“It finally paid off…”
“The police will either treat Kenji as the culprit, or release him once they figure out he’s not who they’re looking for.”
“Either way, they’ll be back to square one.”
“And I’m off the hook…”
“Sure. If you say so.”
“That’s all well and good, but…”
“You’ve been conducting a lot of work recently. Since you stopped living in your apartment.”
“What’s your point?”
“You’ve been logging into Corpse Girl’s website from here. From the factory.”
“You’ve been accessing that Database of the Deceased, too.”
“Don’t you think if the authorities trace that, they’ll just come looking for you here?”
“I’m… I’m using my cell service to connect to the web.”
“I’m not using a dedicated internet connection… And I’m running my connection through a proxy, to mask my IP address…”
“That can’t be traced, right…?”
I shake my head. I’m pretty sure it can be tracked. Not my area of expertise, though.
“Don’t know. But I’d be cautious if I were you.”
“The cops will figure out Kenji’s not guilty soon enough. Just you wait.”
“Normal guy like that… He won’t be able to give them any of the information they’re looking for.”
“Wouldn’t be surprised if he gets released before the weekend.”
“Hitting a dead end like that will only enrage the police. Especially that detective. Fujikawa.”
“Don’t you think they’ll redouble their efforts after that?”
“They’ll surely do whatever it takes to catch the true culprit.”
“Yeah, sure, I hear you, but…”
“Corpse Girl really isn’t the one they’re looking for. The Human Removal Service is behind most of the recent deaths…”
“They don’t know that. They only have eyes for Corpse Girl.”
“You made her famous. Made her known in every household across Tokyo.”
“She’s as much at fault as The Human Removal Service, and you know it.”
“If they catch you… Let’s just say you won’t be let off the hook so easily.”
Noriko folds her arms across her chest angrily.
Not my fault she doesn’t want to hear the truth.
This whole conversation has given me a headache. All my assumptions on the identity of the Herald led me to a brick wall.
But I did glean one interesting piece of information from Noriko’s words.
A phrase that loops within my mind. Verbatim.
‘When Corpse Girl first told me to start killing…’
I rub my chin in thought.
“Gotta go.”
“You good here?”
Noriko drains the rest of her coffee and tosses the can aside.
“Yeah. I’m fine.”
“Later, then.”
Noriko doesn’t speak another word.
I leave in silence.
Got a few hours before I need to be at the morgue.
Usual night shift.
Not a good combination with an early morning.
At least there are no deliveries to make today. For Noriko. Or… For Corpse Girl.
For the best.
If Tomoe is quitting the business, we won’t have a driver.
Didn’t really think that through when I encouraged her to go with her gut.
Oh well. That’s on Noriko. She’s the brains behind the operation.
I’m simply the muscle. Just like I always tell her.
Corpse Girl told Noriko to kill people.
That’s what she said. That’s what Noriko… What Corpse Girl…
That’s what the person I know as Noriko told me.
That begs a follow-up question.
If Noriko isn’t Corpse Girl…
Then who is?
Is Corpse Girl a person? Someone whispering instructions in Noriko’s ear?
Has that always been the case…?
Was I so blindsided by Noriko’s ambitions for grandeur that I disregarded the truth behind her words?
Is Noriko nothing but a puppet?
Too many questions...
Doubt Noriko will willingly spell it out for me. Not if she’s gone to such lengths to mask the truth for so long.
‘When Corpse Girl first told me to start killing…’
I can’t get the quote out of my head.
Too many moving pieces in this puzzle.
Noriko. Corpse Girl. The Human Removal Service. The Herald.
Junpei Matsumoto, and Kenji Ogawa…
Too many assumptions. Too many shadowy figures.
Makes me angry.
Don’t like it when I don’t understand something.
I’m clever. Sharp. Like to know everything.
Like to predict what’s going to happen next.
Like to remain one step ahead of everyone I know.
Right now…
I feel three steps behind. Behind Noriko. Behind whatever Corpse Girl is.
Maybe Tomoe has the right idea. Maybe getting out of this situation is for the best.
Could I really make a clean break?
Could I really just walk away?
Noriko isn’t afraid to play dirty. That has become increasingly more evident, especially with the Kenji situation.
If I walked… Would I have to be on guard for the rest of my life?
Would I have to be cautious of every shadow that flits in the darkness?
Would Corpse Girl come to claim me as her own?
That begs the question…
If Tomoe quits now, will Noriko try to buy her silence with blood?
She’ll do anything to ensure her name isn’t dragged through the dirt.
Tomoe knows too much. As much as me.
She could compromise Noriko’s entire operation if she lets the wrong words slip out in front of the wrong people.
Because of that…
Because of that, I have to believe that Noriko won’t stand for it.
Tomoe’s life will be in danger if she quits now.
I don’t know how. I don’t know by what measure Noriko will strike from the shadows. The girl is weak of body, though strong of mind.
And her ambitions are steeled by some otherworldly force of will.
“Noriko won’t let Tomoe walk away from this.”
Speaking the words aloud and hearing the echo throughout my apartment helps reaffirm the truth.
I have to warn Tomoe.
I don’t know if it’s too late. I don’t know if she’s told Noriko that she’ll be quitting.
But there’s no time to waste.
“Uh… Can I help you?”
“Tomoe in?”
“She’s, uh…”
“Are you a friend of hers…?”
“This is an emergency.”
“Hang on. I’ll go get her.”
I wait patiently as the guy—I assume Tomoe’s boyfriend—goes to fetch her.
It’s fairly late now. The sun is setting. I might miss the start of my shift at the morgue.
This is more urgent.
“What the fuck are yeh doin’ here?”
“Need a word.”
“Mm… How’d yeh get my address?”
“Y’know what? I’d rather not know.”
“Tomoe… Who is this guy? Why does he smell like…”
“Tsk. Long story.”
“Is he bothering you? Should I, um…”
“Should I take care of him?”
My nostrils flare a little as I choke back a laugh.
This guy is pretty scrawny. I’m no martial arts champion, but I find it hard to believe he’d pose a threat to me.
“Nah. It’s all good. He’s harmless, mostly.”
“I see…”
He flashes me an untrusting glare.
“Need to talk. It’s important.”
“Fine. Come in, come in…”
I point a finger at the boyfriend.
“He needs to go.”
“Yes. Come on. What do you think I’m here to talk about?”
“Ugh… Yeah, yeah. Fair point.”
“Shinya, can you, like, clear off for a bit?”
“Tomoe! I want to know what’s going on here!”
“Just who is this guy? Is he an ex-boyfriend of yours?”
“Because… Because, I’ll fight him! You just watch me!”
“No need for that.”
“Not here to steal your girl.”
“Just listen to him, Shinya. Yeh’ve no need to worry.”
“Fine, then! I can tell when I’m not wanted.”
“If anyone needs me, I’ll be outside!”
The boyfriend storms off like an upset toddler and I finally allow myself to crack a smile.
“What a catch.”
“Shut up.”
“Yeh don’t know him like I do.”
Tomoe shuts the front door, leaving us alone in her apartment.
“So what the fuck is this all ‘bout?”
“Need to know. Have you told Noriko you’re quitting?”
“Nah. Not yet.”
“Surely yeh coulda asked me that over noise.”
“Thought you might be in danger already.”
“Danger? Why?”
“Have a theory.”
“Reckon Noriko will cut us up if we leave our merry band.”
“Pfft. Nah. Noriko and I are besties. She wouldn’t hurt me.”
“Don’t act so certain.”
“Noriko will do anything to protect herself.”
“That neighbor of hers? The guy that got arrested?”
“She set him up. From the very start.”
“Made him take the fall so she wouldn’t become a suspect.”
“Yer shittin’ me…”
“Dead serious.”
I take a moment to consider the best way to announce my next theory.
“Don’t think Noriko’s working alone.”
Tomoe simply frowns at what I considered to be a startling revelation.
“Well, ‘course she’s not. We’re workin’ with her.”
Guess I didn’t explain it well enough.
“Not what I meant.”
“Noriko may not be the ringleader here like we assumed.”
“She said, and I quote… ‘When Corpse Girl first told me to start killing…’ End quote.”
Tomoe’s silent contemplation convinces me that I’m onto something. Something that neither of us had stumbled upon previously.
“Well, shit…”
“I thought Noriko was Corpse Girl. She always calls herself that!”
“In fact, she even admitted it to me once! Yeah, I remember it!”
“I kinda suspected it, and I asked her ‘bout it, and she confirmed it.”
“Sure about that?”
“Er, well… Pretty sure, yeah.”
“Eh heh… Now I’m startin’ to doubt myself…”
“Don’t sweat it.”
“Noriko does refer to herself as Corpse Girl. I’m sure of it.”
“Right? I thought so.”
“But… I’m still uneasy about it.”
“Someone convinced her to start killing—and she seems to think it was Corpse Girl.”
“Ugh… I don’t get it…”
“Neither do I.”
“But I’ll get to the bottom of it.”
“For now… For your own safety, don’t tell Noriko you’re quitting.”
“I don’t know how she’ll react.”
“What a drag…”
“I really don’t want to do this anymore…”
“Be patient.”
“Give me a bit of time.”
“Yer sure you can sort this out?”
I’m not exaggerating my confidence. I’m determined to learn the truth. About Noriko—and the identity of Corpse Girl.
Maybe I can figure out why this all started. Why Noriko is so intent on continuing down her path of destruction.
“Leave it to me.”
“Later, then.”
I make my way to the front door and swing it open.
I’m slightly startled when a heavy form stumbles into me.
With his ear pressed up against the door, Tomoe’s boyfriend couldn’t avoid falling forward as the door opened.
I look down at him sprawled on the floor, groaning.
“You okay?”
“He’ll be fine.”
“Get up, Shinya.”
He clambers to his feet and dusts off his trousers.
“I was, uh… Just, um…”
“Got to go. Bye.”
Don’t have time for this.
I push past him and make my way out of the apartment complex.
My late arrival at the morgue is not met by any form of chastisement.
The place is empty. Devoid of life. Nothing out of the ordinary there.
Something is off.
It’s too empty.
Glancing around at the walls of cold chambers, I immediately notice something suspicious.
The majority of the chamber doors aren’t sealed shut.
They’re slightly ajar, as though the last person to access them didn’t close them properly.
I would never do such a thing. I know to press the doors firmly enough that they lock in place.
Leaving a cold chamber unsealed is a surefire way to assist in a cadaver’s deterioration.
And, an unsealed chamber allows the odor of decay to leak into the morgue.
Right now, I don’t smell anything out of the ordinary.
These cold chambers are empty.
Someone has removed the cadavers that were stored inside.
This place was full to the brim just a day ago. There wasn’t a single empty cold chamber.
A cursory glance shows that a good ninety percent of the cold chambers are unsealed.
My initial sense of uncertainty gives way to panic.
I jog toward the left wall of chambers and start pulling the sliding trays out, one by one.
Empty. Empty. Empty.
One after the other.
Each chamber is devoid of its macabre contents.
Even the HRPs have been removed.
I come across one cold chamber that is still sealed. I press the release button in as I pull the handle forward.
The familiar hiss of cold air escaping from the hollow space does little to allay my fears.
I slide the tray out and sigh.
It would seem that even the properly closed chambers have been evacuated.
“Fuck. Shit. Fuck. Shit.”
I dash to the opposite wall. The row of cold chambers that store bodies not due for cremation.
The row that Noriko isn’t allowed access to.
But, just like the other wall, every chamber is empty.
Doors ajar, unsealed, empty.
I thoroughly check each and every one.
“No luck…”
I trudge toward the computer at the far wall.
Logging into the inventory, I scan through the list of recent arrivals and departures.
No bodies came in today. Unusual, but not itself a cause for concern.
More importantly, no bodies have been checked off as removed from the premises.
Each and every body that has disappeared from this place has not been accounted for. The correct protocols have not been adhered to.
I can only draw one conclusion.
The morgue has been robbed.
“Sorry to rock up so late.”
“It’s fine. I was awake.”
“Bad news.”
“Hit me.”
“Morgue’s been plundered.”
“Plundered? What, are you a pirate now?”
“Wait… Your tone. You’re not joking.”
“All the cadavers have been stolen.”
“Cold chambers are completely empty.”
“Yeah, my thoughts exactly.”
“How could you let this happen?!”
“I’m no security guard.”
“Don’t put this on me.”
“How am I supposed to acquire corpses now?!”
“How the fuck am I supposed to appease Corpse Girl?!”
Despite the fact she’s having a Noriko moment, I don’t miss the fear in her voice.
‘Appease Corpse Girl…’
Not something you’d say if referring to yourself.
She’s clearly referring to someone else. Some other being.
Time to put her on the spot.
Sick of always being three steps behind.
“Who’s Corpse Girl?”
“Who is she?”
“Don’t act dense. I’m Corpse Girl.”
“If you’re trying to be funny, it isn’t working. Now isn’t the time.”
“We’ve lost everything, Kojiro.”
“I’ve got a couple of bodies here at the factory, but they’re allocated to victims already.”
“If Corpse Girl gets any new requests, we won’t be able to fulfill them…!”
“There. You did it again.”
“You referred to Corpse Girl as another person.”
“Can you stop messing around?! Don’t you see how serious this is?!”
“I do.”
I do. I see how serious this entire situation has become.
Noriko is delusional.
She refers to Corpse Girl both as herself, and as another person.
She pays no heed to the difference in her words—even when called out on it.
She doesn’t seem to be aware that she’s doing it.
Could be a personality disorder. Can’t place blame on her if that’s the case.
But I think it’s more than that.
She believes she’s being guided, or goaded, by Corpse Girl. Forced to achieve her ambitions.
There’s more to it than a personality disorder.
Something I’m not seeing.
“So. What do we do?”
“Rrrrgh! What can we do?”
“You’ll have to break into another morgue. Start stealing corpses for me.”
“What do you mean, ‘no?!’ Don’t say no to me!”
“I’d do just about anything for you.”
“But sometimes you need to know when to call it.”
“There’s no moving forward from here.”
“I can’t give up, Kojiro.”
“I’ve come so far…”
“Somebody stole the cadavers from the morgue.”
“From my morgue.”
“Somebody who knows what I’m involved in.”
“It wasn’t an attempt to stop what we’re doing.”
“What do you mean…?”
“It was a message.”
“Whoever did it wanted to prove that they are more powerful than we are.”
“Pulling several hundred stiffs from a morgue—all at once—without getting busted…”
“That’s something even we couldn’t achieve.”
“Someone knows our operation. Inside and out.”
“Someone knows what we do, and how we do it.”
“And they wanted to prove that they can do it better.”
“The Human Removal Service.”
“Who else?”
“Damn it…”
“Hope you can see the truth now.”
“We can’t continue with them in the picture.”
“You’re right.”
“Our next move is to destroy them. Destroy the Herald.”
That wasn’t exactly what I was getting at.
I was only trying to discourage Noriko from continuing with her operation.
“What do you propose?”
“You said you’d do nearly anything for me. Right?”
“More or less.”
“Hunt down Junpei Matsumoto. Again.”
“He needs to reveal the identity of his leader. The Herald.”
“Didn’t work so well last time.”
Can’t forget that night. Had the guy beaten and bruised on the ground. Stubborn pup.
“You were interrupted last time.”
“Aoi got in the way, didn’t she?”
“Yeah. Tried to defend her boyfriend.”
“You need to extract information from Junpei at any cost.”
“When you’re done, kill him.”
“I’ve no problem with that.”
“But if Aoi is present again, I’ll have to back down.”
A few seconds of silence makes me ponder if Noriko still has her head in the conversation.
I’m about to repeat myself when she finally speaks.
“If Aoi interferes…”
“Kill her.”
And just like that, Noriko’s true heart is revealed.
She will stop at nothing to achieve her goals.
I was right to fear for Tomoe’s life earlier.
I was right to fear for my own.
If Noriko will cut down her best friend in the world, then she will show no mercy to anyone else.
This kind of resolve… This steel-hearted determination…
I can’t help but admire it.
I respect Noriko.
“If I do this for you…”
“I want something in return.”
“Be with me.”
“You still want me…?”
“I’ve never wanted you more.”
“I’m in love with you, Noriko.”
“In case that wasn’t clear before…”
“Take care of this issue for me, and you can call me yours.”
“I’ll be your girlfriend, or your wife, or your mistress… Whatever you want.”
“My heart will be yours.”
That’s all I wanted to hear.
All I needed to hear.
I don’t want to be alone anymore. I don’t want to feel lonely.
Noriko. Shizuko. Even Tomoe… It doesn’t matter.
I just want somebody to love me. To hold me.
“I’m on it. Leave it to me.”
“Thank you, Kojiro.”
“I’m putting my faith in you.”
I step back. Turn around. Look up. Stare at the stars in the pollution-clouded sky.
When we get together, perhaps we can live in Noriko’s apartment.
My old place.
It will be like coming home after a long absence.
Noriko will replace Shizuko in my heart.
And life will go on.
Text_Month="August 6";Text_Day="THURSDAY";Text_Time="Afternoon"
It’s the same stakeout as last time.
Junpei Matsumoto, in his infinite wisdom, posted on noise about visiting the maid cafe today.
Don’t know why he doesn’t set his profile to private.
Especially after I followed him home last time.
But I won’t be following him again today.
I’ll confront him inside the maid cafe. A place where Aoi is unlikely to be, since she quit the job a while ago.
Although... Did she really quit?
If memory serves, she was dressed as a maid last time I encountered her.
It’s not that I have qualms about killing her.
In fact, I’m not even bothered that Noriko is okay with ordering her death.
I’m just thinking about the future.
When Noriko and I marry, we’ll want friends and family to attend the wedding.
Noriko will need bridesmaids, a maid of honor…
Aoi will be perfect for one of those roles.
By sparing her life now, I can kick off my new life with Noriko on a high note.
I’m aware other people will be present in the cafe.
I’ve no intention of hurting them.
I’ll force as many as possible to evacuate. Or, I’ll corner Junpei somewhere private.
The dog himself arrives as I’m playing through possible scenarios in my head.
He waltzes through the front door, completely oblivious to my presence across the street.
I’ll give him some time.
Let him get comfortable. Lower his guard.
The weight of the blade inside my pocket is unfamiliar. Not like it’s so heavy that it will restrict my movement. Just feels strange.
Figured it was better not to tackle this unarmed. It’s an emergency measure.
After twenty minutes, I approach the maid cafe’s entrance.
Not a fan of the atmosphere.
Too flashy for me. Prefer somewhere more simple. Laid back.
Junpei has a table near the far wall. Alone. Not that I expected any different.
A blonde maid trots over to refill his drink. He nods politely, but doesn’t say a word.
Hasn’t seen me come in yet.
Someone asks if I want a table. I don’t respond.
Someone else chimes in. Something about paying the cover charge.
I don’t know.
My attention is on the dog.
No one attempts to hold me back as I march toward my prey.
He finally sees me, but I’m five steps away and it’s too late.
“Oh, what the…”
“Long time.”
“You’re crazy, man! Get away from me!”
Looking at him up close, he doesn’t seem too worse for wear, considering our last encounter.
I start to wonder if I went too easy on him.
“Can I sit here?”
“Hell no! Get outta here!”
I pull up a chair and sit directly across from him.
The blonde maid from before offers me a menu.
Then she gasps, and I hear something shatter on the floor.
“It’s you…!”
Strange. Aoi didn’t quit her job, after all.
Did she lie to Noriko? Did Noriko lie to me?
I’m ninety-percent sure it’s her, anyway.
“Stay back, babe. I got this.”
Yep. It’s her.
“Thought you quit.”
“I thought you quit this job.”
“What… How would you know that?”
I realize that I shouldn’t spill any details on my relationship with Noriko.
“Forget it.”
“Yo. You think you’re hot stuff, right? Tailin’ me, beatin’ me up…”
“And now you’re diggin’ into my girl’s business?”
“The fuck is wrong with you, man?”
“Excuse me for a second.”
I stand up slightly and lean over the table.
Junpei recoils as my fist pummels his nose.
“Sorry. Had to do it.”
I sit back down and wipe my bloodied knuckles with a napkin.
Junpei clutches his face and sobs. Aoi is visibly shaking, standing next to her dog, unsure how to react.
By some miracle, I don’t think anyone else around witnessed the punch.
For the best. Means we can get down to business without interruption.
“Some questions for you.”
“Fuh… Fuhck… Yeww bwoke my nwose…!”
“Shh. Haven’t asked my question yet.”
Aoi somehow gathers the courage to flee. I don’t watch her leave, but I get the sense she’s gone to fetch help.
“What do you know about the robbery of the hospital morgue?”
“I don’t know what you’re talkin’ about!”
“No. Not the answer I wanted.”
Junpei makes the mistake of possessing fingers.
I jam a steel fork into the back of his left thumb and pin it to the wooden table.
“You’re going to give me the answers I want.”
“Am I clear?”
“You’re a nutcase! You’re a psycho!”
“For my next question…”
“How did you find out about my involvement with Corpse Girl?”
“Haah… Haah…”
It seems that Junpei is carefully weighing his response for the first time.
Instead of outright defiance, he wisely chooses to grant me a satisfactory answer.
“It wasn’t hard, man… You’re not the most stealthy dude around, y’know?”
“You, and that blonde gal girl… Tomoe Watanabe. You’re not cautious enough.”
So. He knows Tomoe’s identity—and her involvement.
This hound is truly a liability.
“It’s not hard to tail you, when you drive that hunk of shit van around town, dropping dead bodies off to Corpse Girl’s targets.”
He knows a lot.
Way too much.
How far does his knowledge extend?
“I see.”
“My next question, then.”
“Do you know Corpse Girl’s identity?”
“Ah ha…!”
“I think the real question is… Do you?”
I consider his words. Do I know Corpse Girl’s identity?
Beginning to doubt that.
Had he asked me a week or two ago, I would have thought of Noriko immediately.
The way that Noriko has been referring to Corpse Girl… I’m not so certain.
But I won’t let this wounded mutt have the upper hand. I won’t let him pry open gaps in my defense.
“Wrong answer.”
The only other piece of cutlery at hand is a metal spoon.
I drive the slightly-pointed rear end of it into the pointer finger on Junpei’s already injured hand.
“Corpse Girl’s identity?”
“Haah… Fine!”
“Noriko… Kurosawa!”
“I see.”
A hesitant tap on my shoulder from behind me causes me to turn.
“Leave… Leave him alone!”
Aoi has somehow gathered a half-dozen other bystanders. They’re all glaring at me, fists clenched, ready to try and forcibly remove me from the premises.
“We’re not done here. Come back later.”
“Let my Junpei go! Stop hurting him!”
For an outwardly meek girl, Aoi has more courage than I expected.
I stand up and stretch my neck.
I’m not looking for a fight with a bunch of cafe patrons.
Heaving a sigh, I dip my hand into my pocket and withdraw the knife.
Flashing it in front of the mob says more than my words ever could.
They all back off, a few letting out snivels of despair.
Aoi, either out of bravery or fear, holds her ground. A single, watery tear welling in her left eye discloses her true feelings.
“Leave. Everyone. Now.”
Doesn’t take more than this animalistic, primitive command to convince the crowd to disperse and rush for the door.
Aoi is amongst the fleeing throng, and she mouths the word ‘sorry,’ as she catches Junpei’s eye.
Satisfied that we will not be interrupted further, I return my attention to Junpei.
He sobs vocally.
“Don’t kill me, man…!”
“I’ll do whatever you want, y’know…”
“Please, I’m beggin’ ya…”
“I’ve got my whole life ahead of me.”
“Only one more question for you.”
“What… What is it…?”
“Who runs The Human Removal Service—who is the Herald?”
“I’m bein’ completely honest with you, man…”
“I don’t know who he is.”
“He wears this creepy-ass mask, and never speaks.”
Can’t quite tell if the dog is being sincere or lying through his teeth.
“I need more than that.”
“Who would know his identity?”
“Look, man…”
“The Human Removal Service…”
“It’s only the two of us!”
“Me, and the Herald… He recruited me online, y’know?”
“He makes me do his legwork!”
“So… If I don’t know who he is, no one does. ‘Cept him, of course.”
Not good enough.
Not the answer I’m looking for.
I lean over the table once more, keeping my knife clearly within the dog’s vision.
“Not happy with that answer.”
“Pick a finger.”
“Shit…! No, dude, seriously! Ask me a different question!”
“Please! Please!”
A voice I didn’t expect to hear rings out from behind me.
“Why are you here?”
“I overheard everything. It’s enough information to use.”
“Is it?”
Noriko strides forward.
It’s a little unnerving seeing her in the real world, away from the factory. She’s been cooped up there for so long.
Her pale skin looks almost otherworldly beneath the cafe’s gaudy lights.
For whatever reason, she’s wearing her best clothes. They’re almost clean, as though she recently did her own laundry.
She walks with purpose, one foot in front of the other, but her gait is unsteady and she is visibly trembling.
At the end of her path, she rests her palms against Junpei’s table and takes a calming breath.
“You stole the corpses from the morgue.”
Noriko doesn’t miss a beat as she flashes her phone at Junpei.
I can’t see what’s displayed on the screen, but the dog hangs his head almost immediately.
“It was me.”
“I robbed the morgue.”
Noriko pockets her phone. She then tosses a small bundle of bandages onto the table.
Junpei hastily grabs the offering with his good hand.
“Get out of here.”
“Get Aoi to bandage you up.”
“And not a word of this to the police.”
With a great deal of effort and a grimace, Junpei plucks the cutlery from his pierced hand and yelps.
Not daring to remain in my presence any longer, he bolts toward the door.
“We’re just letting him go?”
“Don’t understand.”
“You don’t need to.”
Don’t like that.
Don’t feel comfortable not knowing what’s going on.
“What did you show him on your phone?”
“Leave it, Kojiro.”
“Put the knife away. We’re leaving.”
I obey her orders, returning the knife to my pocket.
I follow her unsteady lead and we exit the empty maid cafe.
Noriko gasps unhealthily as she quickly consumes her weight in water.
With a loud swallow, she brings her sleeve to her lips and wipes her mouth dry.
The empty water bottle clatters against the concrete, and Noriko’s gaze returns to me.
“That’s a bit better.”
The visit to the maid cafe got the better of her.
She spent too much energy intervening in the confrontation.
But her motives for doing so remain unclear.
“Fill me in.”
“There’s no need to kill Junpei.”
“Why? He knows everything.”
“Knows me. Knows Tomoe.”
“He knows… You.”
Noriko hesitates, but she doesn’t flinch at the revelation. Something tells me she already knew this much.
“Junpei Matsumoto will be dead by sunrise.”
“I made a request, Kojiro.”
A request?
The first thought that jumps out at me is that she requested for Corpse Girl to kill Junpei Matsumoto.
But that’s a ridiculous notion. Isn’t it?
“I see.”
“I don’t think Corpse Girl can take care of him.”
“He knows our whole operation.”
Noriko’s raised eyebrow conveys her confusion.
“What? No. I didn’t make a request through Corpse Girl’s website.”
“What would be the point of that?”
I shrug, because I truly don’t know what else she could have meant.
“I used the other website.”
“...The Human Removal Service.”
“I made a request for the death of Junpei Matsumoto.”
But, again, what good would that do?
Junpei is an accomplice. If his colleague—the venerable, supposedly immortal Herald—receives a request to kill him, it will simply be ignored.
A startling realization dawns on me.
“Shit. Of course. Why didn’t I suggest that?”
A haunting smirk is inscribed across Noriko’s features.
She knows that I have finally drawn the same conclusion.
“The Herald is ambitious. His convictions are strong. Absolute.”
“Just like mine. Like Corpse Girl’s.”
“Corpse Girl’s convictions, huh…”
“Corpse Girl would never reject a request.”
“That’s right.”
“Junpei Matsumoto is disposable. A pawn.”
“The Herald will deal death to him in the same manner as any other nameless victim.”
“I see.”
“But… More important than Junpei being killed is what we will discover in the aftermath.”
“By knowing that Junpei is the next to be targeted, we can observe him and witness the Herald’s killing method firsthand.”
It’s brilliant.
Noriko has laid the perfect trap.
By sparing Junpei’s life today, we have set him up to be slaughtered by his own compatriot.
And we can use his death as a means to uncover exactly how the Herald brings low his victims.
“Have to hand it to you.”
“This is a pretty fantastic plan.”
“I know.”
“A few things…”
“You have doubts?”
“Not doubts, exactly.”
“Firstly. How do we know exactly when Junpei will be killed?”
Noriko sweeps her hair behind her ear and scoffs, as though the answer should be as clear to me as it is to her.
“I specifically requested the time of death.”
“You can do that?”
“The Human Removal Service demands it.”
“Second topic.”
“What if you’re wrong?”
“What if the Herald isn’t willing to kill his own ally?”
“In that case, it will prove something important.”
“It will prove that we’re dealing with a complete amateur.”
“Someone whose convictions could never reach the strength of Corpse Girl’s.”
And just like that, Noriko reaffirmed my earlier suspicions.
Corpse Girl truly would destroy her own allies in order to see her ambitions fulfilled.
Tomoe. Myself. Our souls are shackled to Corpse Girl’s own black void, yet we are not safe from her wrath.
Should Noriko will it, our flames will be snuffed out in moments.
We are nothing to her. Dirt. Dust.
We will be blown away like the useless, incinerated remains of a cadaver.
“Let’s uncover the secrets behind The Human Removal Service.”
Text_Month="August 7";Text_Day="FRIDAY";Text_Time="Morning"
Another early morning.
If you can call it that. Haven’t gone to sleep yet, so it still feels like late night.
Noriko has me on a short leash. Think she knows it, too.
Apparently she specified this as the place of Junpei’s death. Don’t know how she knew of it.
This parking complex belongs to Junpei’s apartment building. It extends two or three levels underground.
Again, Noriko specified the exact location of the death.
The Human Removal Service seems to take user requests very seriously.
“How much further in?”
“Shh. Keep your voice down.”
“I’m just looking for a good vantage point that we can hide—”
Her words are severed by a violent gasp.
Unable to speak another word, she simply points.
My eyes obediently follow the direction of her slender finger.
“Disappointing. Missed the main event.”
Junpei Matsumoto is already dead.
He’s floating in a sea of his own lifeblood.
Vicious stab wounds practically glow red along his back.
After examining his remains, I turn my attention to the less interesting figure standing motionless beside him.
The masked stranger looks like the villain from a B-rated slasher film.
He’s covered from head to toe in dark clothing. A zipped up jacket with extra long sleeves, a hood, a skirt…
The cut of the figure’s clothes combined with his physique gives me the impression that he may in fact be female.
Is this the Herald we’ve been searching for?
The bloody corpse at her feet would suggest that it is so.
“That mask…”
The mask…?
It’s simple. White. Probably porcelain.
It’s reminiscent of something. Some fictional character, or maybe some film villain, after all.
The Herald still hasn’t moved.
She’s as still as a statue, gaze vacant, her eyes impossible to discern behind the mask.
“Are you the Herald?”
For the first time, the figure moves.
It’s a startling, jerky motion, like a mannequin or a puppet being pulled by strings.
Her head cocks to the side and she seems to notice our presence for the first time.
But an answer to Noriko’s question is not forthcoming.
I step up to the plate.
“You really immortal?”
The Herald doesn’t react to my voice like she reacted to Noriko’s. She has returned to a stiff, doll-like state.
Pretty easy to prove if someone—or something—is immortal. And I’ve always had a curious mind.
I draw the knife from my pocket and launch it at the mannequin.
The blade embeds itself in the thing’s shoulder, and she doesn’t so much as flinch as a trickle of blood pools around the shining steel.
“Missed her heart.”
“Kojiro…! Why did you do that?!”
I shrug and take a step toward the Herald, before Noriko tugs at my coat and holds me back.
She takes my place and puts herself between me and the Herald.
“Tell us who you are. We deserve to know that much.”
Something in Noriko’s words—the sound of her voice, or the tone of her plea—causes the Herald to move once more in acknowledgement.
But the motion this time is quick. Fast, calculated.
The Herald moves a sleeved hand to withdraw the knife from her shoulder, and she allows the blade to drop down to the concrete ground with a dull ‘ting.’
Before the knife hits the ground, the Herald turns her back to us and breaks into a sprint.
“Shit. Not cut out to chase her.”
“Don’t bother. We won’t catch up.”
The Herald disappears into the darkness of the parking lot.
We are left standing by the corpse of Junpei Matsumoto.
“We didn’t see the killing, but…”
“At least the request was granted.”
She’s right. Her gambit paid off.
The Herald killed her own ally.
She has proven her convictions are strong.
I crouch down to examine Junpei’s corpse, but it’s hard to get a good look in the darkness.
Regardless, it’s clear that the dog is dead.
“Should we leave the body?”
“Going to send a text.”
“Huh? Who are you messaging?”
“See if I can pull a few strings. Wouldn’t mind if the corpse ended up at my morgue.”
“What are you planning?”
“Nothing. Really.”
“Just want to prod and poke a bit.”
Noriko’s subsequent grunt is a clear indication that she doesn’t fully believe me.
“Do what you want.”
“I’ve gained as much from this as I had hoped.”
I let her trail off as I turn my attention to my phone.
I swipe through my contacts and quickly compose a message to a few people in particular.
If all goes well, an investigation team will shortly arrive to examine this scene.
I’ll be gone by then. But…
If my contacts do their jobs correctly, they’ll haul Junpei back to the morgue.
I pocket my phone and scurry toward the blood-soaked knife I launched at the Herald.
It slides back into my pocket and I signal to Noriko that we should depart.
“Goodbye, Junpei Matsumoto.”
She waves half-heartedly at the corpse and lets out a child-like giggle.
A scant few hours sleep didn’t offer much in the way of refreshment.
Have to be at the morgue again in an hour.
Not that there’s much to do there since the place was robbed.
Perhaps a few more cadavers will have arrived.
Perhaps Junpei Matsumoto’s corpse will be there.
I should take this opportunity to take a breath.
Been a while since life slowed down like this.
No requests coming through for Corpse Girl.
No bodies to haul around town with Tomoe.
No cadavers to catalogue at the morgue.
Life should be good.
I’m still alone.
And Noriko may decide to discard me at any moment.
Why does that make me want her more?
Do I want to prove my worth? My value?
Prove to her that I’m worth keeping around?
Don’t know.
Doesn’t matter in the long run.
After brewing myself a cup of coffee using the French press Tomoe gifted me, I take a seat in my chair.
Sitting alone in the darkness is somewhat depressing.
But it’s only temporary.
I won’t be alone forever.
Soon, Noriko will sit here with me.
We’ll be together. Together in the darkness.
I’ll make her see my worth.
I’ll make her love me the way that I love her.
I’ll make her fill the void that Shizuko left in my life.
I’ll make her treat the gnawing pain in my insides.
I’ll make her save me from falling into despair. From falling into old habits.
Noriko will save me from myself. Just like Shizuko once did.
I take a sip of my coffee. It’s still a little hot and it scalds the gap in my mouth where my tooth once was.
It hurts.
But I’ll be okay.
It’s hard to hide a smile when plans unfold perfectly.
The body was here, waiting for me, when I arrived at the morgue.
Staring down at the pallid corpse of Junpei Matsumoto fills me with more satisfaction than I thought possible.
The dog is dead, and my early morning encounter with his executioner wasn’t just some fever dream born from wishful thinking.
His body is riddled with stab wounds. Deep, clean, piercing cuts.
But these injuries were not inflicted by a knife.
I’m no forensic pathologist, but…
The wounds are too thin and too deep. Each intrusion is about the width of a chopstick.
Doubt he was killed by chopsticks. Though… You never can rule out everything.
My gaze pans down his body, looking for anything of interest.
The rest of his form looks ordinary.
Nothing to note.
I’ll zip up the bag for now and return him to his allocated cold chamber.
Might take him out once in a while to have a laugh.
As I raise the zipper, covering his legs and groin, I have to shift his arms to fit them within the HRP.
And then I flinch, and my hands instinctively retract from the cadaver.
I’m used to the ice cold touch of a body fresh from its containment chamber. The sensation of lifeless, preserved flesh.
Thus, it wasn’t the sensation of touch that caused me to startle.
It was the sight of something out of the ordinary, something I’d somehow missed during my initial observation.
Junpei’s fingers.
Five thick, meaty digits on each hand.
Ten perfectly intact, dead-but-otherwise-healthy fingers.
It was only days ago that I pierced two of his fingers—his thumb and his pointer finger—using cheap metal cutlery.
I can’t forget the distinct feeling of plunging those implements through flesh and bone, pinning his fingers to a table.
The corpse before me shows no evidence of ever being injured in such a manner.
Nobody can heal wounds like that without medical attention. Even then, stitches and scars will remain.
But Junpei Matsumoto’s digits are one hundred percent intact and puncture-free.
Come to think of it, didn’t I snap another few of his fingers in half that time I confronted him outside his apartment?
I’m sure I did. Crushed the bones within my own fist.
But this corpse’s hands don’t show signs of that, either.
Normal to the touch. No visible bruising.
On a whim, I pull out my phone and open noise.
I navigate to Junpei Matsumoto’s profile.
Load a few profile images. Swipe through them one-by-one.
I put my phone right next to Junpei’s head, comparing the similarities between Junpei’s photos and his dead body.
Everything becomes clear immediately.
Certain elements of Junpei’s features don’t match.
His nose is broader in photos. His lips are thinner, more taut.
The corpse in front of me is not Junpei Matsumoto.
It’s a copy.
A clone.
Junpei Matsumoto’s death was faked for our entertainment.
The body lying on the ground in front of the Herald was planted there before we arrived. Planted to convince us that Junpei had met his maker.
The Herald did not kill Junpei. The Herald simply used one of Corpse Girl’s tricks and produced a carbon-copy body.
All in order to fool myself and Noriko.
As this revelation settles in my mind, I come to another conclusion.
The morgue being robbed was no coincidence. I can almost guarantee that the cadaver used to replicate Junpei’s death was stolen from this very place.
A weapon of deception, stolen and turned against us.
And, the morgue was targeted before Noriko even requested Junpei’s death.
Almost as if The Human Removal Service predicted Noriko’s movements in advance.
Is that even possible?
All I know for sure is that the dog is still out there. Still skulking around, working for his master.
This is starting to get interesting.
Text_Month="August 8";Text_Day="SATURDAY";Text_Time="Afternoon"
“Okay. I think I’m up to date.”
“I guess it was a good thing you decided to ‘prod and poke’ Junpei’s corpse, as you put it.”
“Guess so.”
“I thought you were just being your usual morbid self. Taking corpses for your own use—whatever that may be.”
“Don’t know what to tell you.”
“Well, I’m glad you acted.”
“Faking Junpei’s death…”
“What’s their end goal?”
“What did they really accomplish by pulling such a stunt?”
There’s a million possible answers to that question.
Can’t know the real truth. Not yet.
“Obvious answer would be that they wanted to deceive us.”
“Make us think we have the upper hand.”
“I came to the same conclusion.”
“They think they’ve fooled us.”
“But we know better. Can we use that to our advantage?”
“Don’t know.”
“Sometimes you’re helpful, and other times you’re just…”
“Never mind.”
It irritates her when I withhold my thoughts.
Sometimes I act like this just to elicit a reaction from her.
She’s cute when she’s pissed off.
“I don’t know what we should do next.”
“We’re kind of at a dead-end, right?”
“Kind of.”
“Corpse Girl’s website has gone silent. No one is requesting deaths anymore.”
“But… If I’m to believe the news, there are still dozens of people being killed all around the city.”
“Which means… The Human Removal Service is still as active as ever.”
“Don’t beat yourself up."
“Don’t have any cadavers at the morgue, anyway.”
“Can’t exactly fulfill any requests.”
She sighs and rubs her eyes.
Despite her tired, exhausted appearance, she’s dealing with recent events rather well. For Noriko, at any rate.
“Can you let me know when the morgue starts filling up again?”
“Hang on. There is one body there.”
“Fake Junpei.”
“Not much use though, I suppose.”
“No. Not really.”
“Keep me updated.”
She rubs her eyes again and tries to hold back a yawn.
“You look wrecked.”
“Things are tough right now…”
“It’ll get better.”
“You’ll cause some deaths soon enough.”
My words have the strange effect of actually cheering her up slightly.
I know we’re not exactly the most normal people.
The things we do, the causes we devote ourselves to…
They are wrong.
There’s no other way to put it.
I know this. I trust that Noriko knows this as well.
We’re morbid. Sick. Disgusting.
Noriko slaughters innocent people in the name of Corpse Girl. Her fabricated idol, or alter-ego, or whatever else she could be.
As for me…
I’ve got as much blood on my hands as Noriko does.
She likes to believe she’s innocent, but the truth is that she’s just as guilty as any killer.
I don’t see myself the same way. I know for a fact the things I’ve done are enough to put me behind bars for the rest of my life.
I don’t try to convince myself that I’m something I’m not. I’m a criminal, plain and simple.
Noriko is a kindred spirit. We’re connected on some level that I don’t expect the average person to understand.
We’re bonded by the things we’ve done. The death we’ve witnessed.
Looking at her now, this tired girl worn thin by stress...
I can’t help but be reminded of Shizuko.
I messed up with Shizuko. I didn’t take the time we had together seriously.
I took it all for granted.
I won’t make the same mistake with Noriko.
I’ll make her mine, and I’ll prove my love to her every day.
Perhaps that will convince her to not discard me when I’ve run out of use.
“Want something to eat?”
She glances at me and opens her mouth, but weighs her words before speaking.
“Thanks, but…”
“You know me.”
“I know.”
Of course I know.
I know so much about her.
